Football.title: Top flight league officially becomes first to trial Arsene Wenger’s new daylight offside rule
Football.content:
ARSENE WENGER’s new offside rule is going to trial in a top flight football league for the first time.

The former Arsenal manager’s controversial daylight offside rule, mandated for a test run by Fifa and Ifab, will be implemented in the Canadian Premier League this season.



The rule itself dictates there needs to be a complete gap between the attacker and the second-to-last opposition player.



And the CPL will be the first top league in the world to play with the rule.

League CEO, James Johnson, said of the decision: “This is about positioning the Canadian Premier League at the forefront of innovation and contributing meaningfully to the global evolution of the game,”

“By working closely with Fifa and Ifab, we are proud to play a role in shaping the future of football while continuing to build a competition that reflects our ambition here in Canada.”

The Wenger offside law will be implemented with the addition of a new Football Video Support (FVS) system.

FVS will allow officials to review key incidents using available broadcast footage with the support of qualified Replay Operators.

Unlike VAR seen in the Premier League and across Europe, there will be no dedicated video match official.

Wenger, now Fifa’s Chief of Global Football Development, added: “This is an important pilot.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“By testing this new interpretation in a professional competition, we can better understand its impact, including in terms of improving clarity and the flow of the game and promoting attacking play.



“We look forward to analysing the results of the trial phase.

“We thank the Canadian Premier League and the Canadian Soccer Association for their willingness to support Fifa with this pilot and for providing their competition.”

Furthermore, reviews will be initiated by coaches with a limit of two video review requests per match for match-changing situations, including goals, penalty decisions, direct red cards and cases of mistaken identity.

If a review results in a decision being overturned, then the team will retain the opportunity to use the review again.

The CPL are also bringing new rules to stop time wasting and improve match tempo to the table.



These measures include a five-second countdown if a throw-in or goal-kick is viewed as being delayed, subs being made to leave the pitch within 10 seconds and players being required to leave the field for one minute when receiving medical treatment.

The CPL season, the eighth season since the league’s foundation, starts on April 4.

Football.title: Forgotten Man Utd keeper ready to challenge Lammens after going viral and bouncing back from De Gea disaster
Football.content:
CORNERS NOW resemble the jostling at a Boxing Day sale. But Manchester United have another goalkeeper who can deal with them.

“It is difficult for goalkeepers but luckily for me, I am 6ft 5in,” Radek Vitek says. “So I can deal with that.





“I like to come for crosses and help my team-mates by claiming them or punching them away from dangerous areas.”

Vitek, 22, is enjoying a fine season-long loan at Bristol City, where he has started in 34 Championship games.

Before our chat, he went viral with a triple-save at Middlesbrough, where Vitek’s near-post run at a corner contributed to City’s 96th-minute equaliser.

Initially signed to provide cover for No1 and Ireland international Max O’Leary, a pre-season injury to O’Leary allowed Vitek to take his place and he has barely looked back.



“It was a difficult task to keep the shirt but in the back of my mind, I always wanted to stay here and play the whole season,” Vitek tells Sun Sport. “That was my goal.

“At this stage in my career, at a young age, I want to play as many games as possible. I wouldn’t benefit from sitting on the bench here, or anything else.”

Vitek will find one of football’s most familiar faces at Bristol City’s Robins High Performance Centre taking training this week.

At the age of 78, Roy Hodgson has taken the plunge at the second-tier side after Gerhard Struber was sacked.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

This is Czech talent Vitek’s third loan and United extended his contract to 2028 to coincide with his latest temporary move.

The working approach at United is that any Championship loanee is regarded as genuine first-team potential.

Dean Henderson helped Sheffield United to Premier League promotion in 2019 before he returned to compete with David de Gea the following year.

Vitek, similarly to Henderson, would be reluctant to go back to United just to provide cover for Senne Lammens. He is open to another Championship loan.

“At the moment, I’m focussing on the end of the season and finishing as strong as possible for Bristol City with eight games to play,” he explains.



“I just want to give my best for the club and to build my platform towards next season.

“I will communicate with Man United closely and we will see what’s going to be best for me next season.



“But I want to play football. I don’t want to just be somewhere sitting on the bench.

“I really appreciate the trust [United] are giving me. Obviously, I am going step by step.”

Vitek stresses United have been “really good” in overseeing his development. He is in constant dialogue with Craig Mawson, the club’s goalkeeping coach.

Mawson watches clips of Vitek’s performances and provides feedback from afar.

Vitek was 13 when he left his hometown of Vsetín to join the Sigma Olomuc academy 80 kilometres away.



By the time of his arrival as a 16-year-old at United in the summer of 2020, the world had been turned upside down by the Covid-19 pandemic.

“I couldn’t turn down Manchester United at such a young age,” he stresses. “I knew it would be a challenge; new country, new language.

“But if you don’t work for something in life, you can’t achieve much. Looking back, I did the right thing. It builds my personality and character as well.

“You speak about mentality; when you work hard every day towards something, towards the weekend, you feel much better and more confident.

“There have been some difficult times but when you overcome that, it builds you up, you have more confidence and you believe in yourself.



“I have always been a bit of a loner because I moved from my hometown at a really young age to play for Sigma Olumuc, which was over an hour from my home.

“I stayed over the week some days, so I was already used to the travel and being on my own.

“But I have graduated to a different level.

“When I came to Man United first, I wasn’t anywhere near the agility level or movement level where I am now.



“So I have to thank all the academy staff and goalkeeper coaches for what they done with me. I feel like a massive improvement since age 16 to that first loan.

“So one of the best academies in the world helped me in my career.”

As a fellow Czech, Vitek is in awe of Petr Cech: “He was one of the best goalkeepers in the world. He set records in the Premier League, the best league in the world, which says everything really.



“You can look at him as an example from a young age for me.

“I try to look at as many goalkeepers because everyone is good at something different.

“I could say Manuel Neuer, for what he has done in that position over the years.”

Vitek has worked his way up the English football pyramid, having kept goal for Accrington Stanley in League two in 2024.

That preceded a season-long loan with Austrian side Blau-Weiß Linz but Vitek was keen on securing an English loan for this season.



The Championship remains one of the most enthralling leagues in Europe.

“The main difference (with League Two) is the quality of the players are more tactic-wise,” Vitek says.

“I remember in League 2 it was more like a dogfight! You literally go long and everyone was just scrapping for the second balls.

“But here in the Championship, obviously it’s more tactical, every team plays different balls or some more combinations, so you have to adjust.”

Vitek has made the United bench seven times, usually in European games when matchday squads are extended to 23 players.



He has trained with David de Gea, Andre Onana and Tom Heaton, observing how their pre-match preparations differ.

His maiden first-team appearance was a memorable one against Wrexham in San Diego on the 2023 pre-season tour.

United’s starting ‘keeper, Nathan Bishop, was involved in a collision with Wrexham hero Paul Mullin, who suffered a punctured lung.

The Californian Wrexham fans booed Bishop, who was replaced by Vitek at half-time. Vitek was also then booed, with thousands unaware there had been a change in goal.



Vitek shone in a 1-0 defeat to Rosenborg at the start of United’s pre-season schedule in 2024 but the plan was always for him to head out on loan.

His only Old Trafford appearance was in the 2022 FA Youth Cup final against Nottingham Forest. Michael Carrick was invited back by United for the game to recognise his work with their academy talents.

Vitek and Carrick’s paths briefly crossed. “I think I was with him shortly, maybe when Ole (Gunnar Solskjaer) was in the club.

“I went for a few trainings with the first team but it was a long, long time ago!”



Vitek’s career progress is all the more admirable as he committed an error in that final triumph with United 1-0 up.

67,492 supporters – a record crowd in the Youth Cup – watched as Vitek fumbled a daisy-cutter into the Stretford End net. De Gea, sitting in the directors’ box, looked on glumly.

Two team-mates pulled Vitek back to his feet as he resembled a mole attempting to burrow itself into the ground.

It is to Vitek’s immense credit that he has recovered from that public error and is one of three members from that starting XI still at United. The other two are Kobbie Mainoo and Dan Gore.

“Yeah, massive,” Vitek recalls of the mistake. “To overcome some mistakes, it makes you much stronger.



“And I think I proved, season by season or after that moment. Even now this season, I’ve made some mistakes.

“But then when I go to the next game and do well, help the team, then it allows me to grow, personality-wise and self-confidence.”

He can deal with that, too.

Football.title: How Sky Sports can break own TV rule to move matches with Man Utd worst hit – and two teams unaffected
Football.content:
SKY SPORTS have been able to break their own TV rules over selections for Monday and Friday night football by swapping teams where necessary.

The broadcaster is only supposed to pick a team to play on Monday or Friday night a maximum of five times across a Premier League season.





But a handful of teams have moved past that figure with Manchester United the worst affected on eight games.

Everton and West Ham are both on seven games, while Leeds United have reached six.

The Everton Fan Advisory Board has hit out at the team’s constant broadcast changes after their clash against Man City in May was moved from a Saturday to a Monday.

They said: “The decision to move yet another home fixture to a Monday evening, the seventh such change this season, is yet another signal of the disregard footballing authorities and broadcasters have for football supporters.



“We fully understand the commercial realities and importance of broadcasting revenues. However, the cumulative effect of these decisions is now materially damaging supporter accessibility, matchday experience, and long-term engagement.

“We will be raising the concerns of Evertonians directly with the broadcasters and the Premier League.”

United, meanwhile, said it would “advocate on behalf of fans” over the issue, but added: “Our fixtures are available for broadcast picks at times when other clubs are not.”

The Premier League made 270 out of 380 games available for broadcast this season, with Sky holding four of the five packages available.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

According to the BBC, Sky can give themselves more flexibility with the five-maximum rule by swapping the day and time of games.

For example, if a club was scheduled to play on a Monday night but couldn’t play due to a Champions League game, Sky could switch them with Everton’s Saturday match.

That wouldn’t count towards Everton’s five-game total because they were not initially picked for Monday in the first place.

The report claims that the rule of five games is a “loose limit” because of the constantly changing situation around matchday broadcasts.



SunSport has reached out to Sky Sports for comment.

Arsenal and Tottenham are the only teams to have zero games selected for Friday or Monday night broadcast.

Both teams have been in the Champions League this season, helping to shield them from Friday and Monday selection.

Manchester United, meanwhile, weren’t in Europe – which might explain why they have had so many picks.



Tottenham would be high on Sky’s list for Monday and Friday selection next season should they stay in the Premier League because of their high-profile presence.

A look at the TV picks for this season shows that Burnley have had just two Monday/Friday games but have appeared ten times on Saturday 3pm slot at home.

Wolves have had nine 3pm home game slots, with Bournemouth and Brighton both having eight.

Football.title: Bruno Fernandes, Jordan Pickford and Jarrod Bowen among most in-form Dream Team players
Football.content:
IF the international break has lured you into World Cup fantasies then allow us to provide a reality check.

Two months remain of the 2025/26 Dream Team season and this is no time to lose focus so we thought it would be useful to publish a reminder of which players were in the best form prior to the break.



GOALKEEPERS

Jordan Pickford (£3.3m) is the most in-form keeper having taken 20 points from his last three outings via two clean sheets.



Everton’s 3-0 win over Chelsea in Gameweek 29 was hugely impressive and the Toffees now have their eyes firmly set on European qualification.

England’s No1 has excelled between the sticks this campaign but won’t play in Gameweek 30 as David Moyes’ side are out of the FA Cup.

The same is true of Bournemouth and Dream Team’s second most in-form keeper Djordje Petrovic (£3.3m).

Emi Martinez (£3.9m) and David Raya (£4.2m) rank joint-third in their position in terms of form at present and both are among the minority of custodians with at least one fixture to fulfil immediately after the break.



Aston Villa will travel to Bologna for the first leg of their Europa League quarter-final while Arsenal are scheduled to face Southampton and Sporting CP.

It’s probably overly optimistic to expect Raya to start both games as Kepa Arrizabalga (£2.8m) has started in the domestic cups this season.

That being said, the latter was guilty of a costly error against Manchester City in the Carabao Cup final and so it’s not inconceivable that Mikel Arteta will revert to his No1 at St Mary’s.

Raya is the most popular asset in his position by a wide margin with an ownership of 30.6% — no other keeper feature in more than 8% of teams at the time of writing.



DEFENDERS

Dream Team’s joint most in-form defenders will both be in action in Gameweek 30.

Ethan Ampadu (£3.1m) suffered heartbreak with Wales against Bosnia-Herzegovina but he is on a streak of three consecutive clean sheets with Leeds at club level.

The 25-year-old has banked 27 points in this time and will be hopeful of another shut out against West Ham in the FA Cup this weekend with a place in the semi-finals up for grabs.

Nikola Milenkovic (£3.5m) has also amassed 27 points from his last three appearances.



Nottingham Forest’s tall centre-back contributed to clean sheets against Fulham and Spurs either side of a 13-point haul against Midtjylland.

The Serbia international assisted Nicolas Dominguez’s (£3.1m) opening goal in Denmark and was replaced by Murillo (£3.3m) just after the hour mark with the score at 2-0 to Forest, meaning he registered a clean sheet — the hosts scored soon after before Vitor Pereira’s troops prevailed on penalties.

Milenkovic may be up against it in Gameweek 30 away to Porto in the Europa League quarters as the Portuguese side are favourites to win their top flight this season having only lost one league game all season.

Truth be told, Neco Williams (£4.2m) is the Forest defender of choice as he ranks third in his position overall with a mighty total of 232 points.

The Welsh full-back leads the way among defenders for shots on target and tackles at this stage.



He took Spurs for 17 points before the break and is also among the notable form players.

MIDFIELDERS

Three of the four most in-form midfielders will not play in Gameweek 30.

Owners of Bruno Fernandes (£6.6m), Xavi Simons (£4.7m) and Anthony Gordon (£4.4m) will need to find replacements or make their peace with blanks.

In regards to Manchester United’s talisman, the outright most in-form performer in the game, his recent returns have been so impressive that Dream Team bosses who ditch him for Gameweek 30 may be tempted to bring him back in for Gameweek 31 when the Red Devils will host Leeds.



Conversely, Dominik Szoboszlai (£5.5m) has two fixtures to fulfil in Gameweek 30, albeit a tough double header in the form of Man City (a) and PSG (a).

The Hungarian playmaker has bagged 26 points across his last three outings to take his tally for the season to 290!

He is likely to be the second player to pass the 300-point milestone in 2025/26 — Erling Haaland (£6.6m) was the first.

Szoboszlai is currently the second-most selected midfielder (35.4% ownership) but he might start reeling in Antoine Semenyo (45%) following City’s elimination from the Champions League.

FORWARDS



Igor Thiago (£4m) is the most in-form striker but Brentford are among the teams without a fixture straight after the break.

However, runner-up Jarrod Bowen (£5.4m) is a genuinely good option.

As previously mentioned, Leeds have kept things tight at the back recently but West Ham’s skipper has added 28 points in his last three games via two goals and one assist.

The England international ranks in the top three in his position for assists, big chances created, tackles and bonus points.

The Hammers are prioritising top-flight survival at the back end of this season but they will be up for Sunday’s FA Cup quarter-final in East London.

Bowen is often a smart differential option for gaffers who like to go against the grain.

He currently appears in 4.8% of teams.

Football.title: Usain Bolt in talks to join host of Premier League cult heroes in Sunday League team with ‘silly’ list of players
Football.content:
USAIN BOLT is in talks to join a star-studded over-35s Sunday League team, claims ex-Manchester City star Stephen Ireland.

The former fastest man on the planet, 39, is a huge football fan and supports Manchester United.





Bolt has played in several charity matches down the years, including Soccer Aid.

And now he could lace them up to star alongside the likes of Ireland, Joleon Lescott and Danny Drinkwater.

Chatting to Ladbrokes about Wythenshawe FC, Ireland said: “Every week without fail there’s Danny Drinkwater, Joleon Lescott, Danny Simpson, George Boyd, Papiss Cisse, Oumar Niasse.

“There are loads… the registration list is silly. Then because only 11 can play, I have to tell these ex-pros that we don’t need you for this week and everyone’s like dying to play.

“Some of the Irish lads have registered as well. You got Paul McShane, Darron Gibson, Ciaran Westwood.

“Usain Bolt came out recently saying he wants to come and play with us. So we’re speaking to him at the moment. So yeah, it’s just amazing and I absolutely love it.”

Wythenshawe FC’s exploits have gone viral several times this season, and Ireland has seen interest start to grow.

The Irishman added: “It’s huge. We won two finals in the last two weeks and we’re probably going to win the league.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“But the legs it’s carrying and how much traction it’s got… it’s just exploded. There are massive crowds coming now.

“It’s brilliant and everyone’s really excited. It’s been a great incentive for fitness and socialising and everyone getting together. And also the mental health side of things.

“You come away from football and don’t know what to do with yourself or feel like you have a purpose.



“Even though you try to prepare for that, it’s impossible because one day it’s taken away from you and your routines have been taken away.

“Anyway, we are going to America in May competing for a million dollars in a tournament.

“We’re going to Hong Kong a week before it and there’s so many things lined up.

“Guys are getting jobs off the back of it and doors are opening.

“Some players are getting sponsorship off the back of it, and I guess it’s giving people a real purpose again.”



Bolt’s last Soccer Aid appearance ended in nightmare circumstances.

Football.title: Inside Erling Haaland’s luxury £10million car collection as Man City star buys one of the world’s rarest cars
Football.content:
ERLING HAALAND is one of the fastest players in the Premier League and thanks to his extravagant car collection, he is just as quick off the pitch.

The Manchester City superstar has an array of vehicles with a combined value of more than £10million.



He added to the luxury collection this week with by purchasing an ultra-rare Mercedes supercar worth £400,000.



Haaland, 25, acquired a limited edition Mercedes-Maybach Virgil Abloh – only 150 models exist worldwide.

The left-hand drive car is powered by a massive twin-turbo 6.0L V12 biturbo engine with a top speed of 155mph.

The luxury sedan goes from 0-60mph in 4.5 seconds and is all-wheel drive.

That is slow compared to some of the cars in his garage, with stunning Porsche 911 GT3 capable of 0-60mph in just 2.7 seconds.



Mercedes-Maybach Virgil Abloh, £400,000

The brand new Mercedes is not only the rarest, but also the most expensive item in Haaland’s collection.

The luxury limousine is the final bespoke S-Class variant produced in co-operation with the late Louis Vuitton artistic director who tragically died at age 41 from a rare type of cancer.

The stunning saloon was completed before designer Abloh’s death in 2021 and is now a collector’s item in the super high-end second-hand market.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Car fanatic Haaland managed to bag one of the bespoke cars and was spotted driving it through Alderley Edge, Cheshire.



The supercar features a unique, two-tone exterior colour scheme, with glossy Obsidian Black on the top half of the car, while the lower segment, side flanks and wheel rims feature a sand hue.

Aston Martin DBX 707, £350,000

Haaland also has a taste for SUVs, and his Aston Martin was once the world’s most powerful SUV before the Ferrari Purosangue was made.

But it’s not exactly slow, achieving 0-60 mph in just 3.3 seconds.

So it is no surprise Formula 1 use it as one of their safety cars.



Haaland owns a forest green version, and it looks very sleek and stylish.

Porsche 911 GT3, £160,000

After Haaland created history by penning a 10-year contract with City in January 2025, he was seen behind the wheel of a new car – his beloved Porsche.

And he certainly stood out thanks to the bold orange colour of his new wheels.

The flash sports car is worth £160,000 and reaches 60mph in just 2.7 seconds.



Range Rover Sport, £120,000

On the more modest end of the spectrum, Haaland often drives the classic footballer’s car – a Range Rover Sport.

Back in 2018, it was the most leased car by Premier League stars.

It is a favourite around Manchester for players of City and United, and their wags.

It can manage 0-60 mph in 4.3 seconds and reaches a top speed of 176 mph.



Rolls-Royce Cullinan, £300,000

What car collection would not be complete without a Rolls-Royce.

It is a giant of a car, reaching 5.3m long, 2.1m wide and 1.8m tall.

But that’s not to say the 2.6 tonne Cullinan lacks any power.

Its 6.75-litre twin turbo V12 engine means the giant motor is still capable of hitting 62mph in five seconds with a top speed of 155mph.



The Cullinan is also part of Cristiano Ronaldo’s extensive collection, with boxer Andy Ruiz Jr also owning one.

Audi RS6 Avant, £120,000

Of all his cars the Audi RS6 Avant is the one Haaland drives most.

It has been a favourite of his for a while, too, with the striker driving one during his spell at Borussia Dortmund.

He now owns a carbon black model, which boasts an acceleration of 0 to 60mph in a mere 3.5 seconds.



Mercedes-AMG GLE Coupe, £90,000

The Norwegian’s Mercedes Coupe is yet another SUV in his collection.

It is not short of speed since it takes 5.2 seconds to go from 0-60mph, but it is also the height of luxury.

It’s another regular runner for Haaland to get to training, particularly on days he is feeling less flashy.

Football.title: Premier League club SELLS 52,264-seater stadium to its owners in controversial £172m move amid PSR fears
Football.content:
NEWCASTLE’s owners have revealed they sold St James’ Park to themselves, amid PSR fears.

Toon chiefs David Hopkinson and Simon Capper lifted the lid on the club’s 2024-25 accounts on Tuesday.



It revealed the Magpies enjoyed a record turnover of £335.3million, a £15m increase on the year before.



However, the accounts revealed that the 72-year lease on the club’s home ground was sold to a subsidiary company by the name of PZ Holdings Ltd.

This company falls under the ownership of PIF and the Reuben Brothers, the same bodies who own the club.

It made the club £172.1m, with the 52,264-seater stadium being leased back for the next 50 years.

The decision, which was valued as fair market by the Premier League, allowed the club to book a profit of £129m.

That led to the club being able to register a total after-tax profit of £34.7m instead of the record £98.4m loss that the Toon were facing.

The ‘asset sale trick’ has been used by Chelsea in the past, though in that case BlueCo sold their hotels and women’s team to comply with PSR rules.

There had been concerns that Newcastle would fall foul of PSR, particularly due to the club still carrying a large 2023 debt burden.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, the club insists that the motivation behind the St James’ Park sale was to reorganise assets before any potential stadium development, either at St James’ or elsewhere.



Chief financial officer Capper said: “The motivation was very much to reorganise our property assets and get them into the correct legal boxes to allow us to go forward with our potential development, either at St James’ Park or for a new stadium, and to facilitate that with financing and other similar items.

“There may be more similar transactions to come in the future, depending on what we end up doing.

“But the profit calculation that had to be done is then a consequence of the detail of the accounting rules that the Premier League require us to follow in doing any transaction with a company that is associated with us.

“So it does create a very significant accounting profit because of that.”

The new company who now owns St James’ Park will borrow any capital needed for development, removing the debt burden from Newcastle.



Capper added that the sale does give the club a lot of “PSR headroom”, but admitted most of that would not roll into squad cost due to Uefa regulations not allowing for such accounting tricks to be counted, while PSR is also changing to SCR.

Newcastle look set to lose at least one of their big-name midfielders in the summer with Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes both linked with moves away.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

That follows the record-breaking £125m sale of Alexander Isak to Liverpool last summer, which chief executive Hopkinson told reporters was a “good sale” in terms of extracting the maximum from a transfer.

Chief exec Hopkinson also spoke about Eddie Howe‘s future, admitting the club had no set stance on his future but they were not looking to make a change now.

Football.title: Former Premier League star demands new rule to suspend TEN Arsenal players – ‘doesn’t sit right with me’
Football.content:
GABBY AGBONLAHOR says Premier League players should be suspended for their next game if they withdraw from internationals.

Arsenal stars have come under fire after TEN players returned to the club early over various injury concerns.





Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice both pulled out of England’s clash against Japan on Tuesday.

Noni Madueke also withdrew after picking up an issue in the 1-1 draw with Uruguay and England boss Thomas Tuchel defended the group.

He insisted Saka and Rice were “genuinely injured” but understood it looked “suspicious” amid their Premier League title bid.

But Agbonlahor said the spate of withdrawals “isn’t right” and called on top flight chiefs to come down harder on players.



But he criticised Saka, Rice, Piero Hincapie, Gabriel, William Saliba, Leandro Trossard and Zubimendi for pulling out over the international break.

He insisted harsher punishments are needed to deter players from leaving their countries.

The ex-Aston Villa star told talkSPORT: “(Noni) Madueke, no problem, you pulled out, you got injured against Uruguay, it was quite a hard tackle.

“I look at players like (Jurrien) Timber, (Eberechi) Eze, (Martin) Odegaard, all pulled out because they didn’t play against Manchester City. Those four players, no problem with it.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“But (Piero) Hincapie, (Bukayo) Saka, (Declan) Rice, Gabriel, (William) Saliba, (Leandro) Trossard, (Martin) Zubimendi had no problems against Manchester City. I just don’t think it’s right.

“If I was part of the Premier League and I was making a decision, I would bring in a new rule, you miss the next Premier League game available if you pull out of international duty. I tell you something, players will stop pulling out.”

He also called on Three Lions skipper Harry Kane to put a stop to withdrawals after the Bayern Munich star previously called players out in 2024.

Agbonlahor added: “Playing for your country is an honour. If I’m Harry Kane, I’m speaking about this and saying, ‘Come on, guys, let’s not go back to what we were doing four or five years ago where players are pulling out non-stop.’



“I get it, (Mikel) Arteta is doing everything possible to win these trophies. Their next game after the international break is the FA Cup against Southampton.

“I’m just not keen on players pulling out of international duty. It’s an honour to play for your country. It doesn’t sit right with me.”

Arsenal’s injury worries come at a time when they are seven points clear of rivals Man City, who are nine points behind their rivals with a game in hand.

The Gunners have seven games to go but face City in a crucial title-defining game at the Etihad on April 19.

Football.title: Why England's opponents have sacked their manager 72 days before 2026 World Cup
Football.content:
Why England's opponents have sacked their manager 72 days before 2026 World Cup

England will face Ghana on June 23 at the World Cup finals, but the African nation have sacked head coach Otto Addo following back to back losses against European nations

View Image Otto Addo gives Antoine Semenyo instructions during the defeat to Germany, hours before being sacked as Ghana boss (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Ghana have sacked their coach Otto Addo - just 72 days before the start of the World Cup. The Black Stars are England’s second Group opponents on June 23 but Ghana wielded the axe after a run of four straight defeats.

‌



It also comes after Ghana failed to qualify for the Africa Cup of Nations despite having star names like Antoine Semenyo and Mohammed Kudus. Ghana lost 2-1 to Germany in Stuttgart just days after being thrashed 4-1 by Austria last Friday night and four straight defeats signalled the end of Addo’s second spell in charge.

‌



Former Borussia Dortmund midfielder Addo, 50, led Ghana to the last World Cup and was re-appointed in March 2024 but lost nine of his 22 games in charge.

‌



There had been a big fan backlash and Addo was sacked just hours after the Germany defeat - despite the home side needing an 88th minute winner from Deniz Undav to secure victory. Ghana had also lost to Japan and South Korea in November.

A Ghana FA statement read: “The Ghana Football Association will communicate the new technical direction of the Black Stars in due course."

‌



Ghana will open their campaign against Panama on 18 June before facing England in Boston. They end the group stage against Croatia in Philadelphia on June 27, with Ghana FA bosses targeting a place in the knockout stages this summer.

Football.title: Cristiano Ronaldo 'intervenes in Man Utd transfer' to spite Lionel Messi
Football.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo 'intervenes in Man Utd transfer' to spite Lionel Messi

Cristiano Ronaldo is reportedly trying his best to scupper plans that would benefit Lionel Messi

View 2 Images Casemiro is still deciding where he will play his football beyond this summer (Image: PA)

Cristiano Ronaldo is reportedly trying to convince Manchester United star Casemiro to join his Al-Nassr side over Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami this summer. Casemiro, 34, announced in January that he will be leaving United at the end of this season after four years at Old Trafford.

‌



The Red Devils decided not to trigger the 12-month extension in the Brazilian’s four-year contract due to his mammoth £350,000-per-week wages, which they are eager to cut from their wage bill. It emerged last week that one of Casemiro’s potential destinations is Inter Miami, given the MLS side’s recent interest in him.

‌



The opportunity to play with Messi in the United States will undoubtedly be a tantalising prospect for the five-time Champions League winner. But Casemiro’s former Real Madrid team-mate Ronaldo is now reportedly trying to prevent that move from happening.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Spanish publication Marca claims Ronaldo is attempting to persuade Casemiro to snub Messi and instead join the United legend in Saudi Arabia. Ronaldo signed for Al-Nassr in the Saudi Pro League in January 2023, becoming the highest-paid player on the planet.

The Portuguese made the switch from Old Trafford to the Middle East himself after a bitter falling out with then-manager Erik ten Hag and club bosses. Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr currently lead the Saudi top flight in what could be his first league title success with the club, though he is currently out of action with a hamstring injury.

‌



Portuguese media react as Bruno Fernandes left powerless after career first moment READ MORE :

World Cup Legends - special edition on sale now READ MORE :

Messi, meanwhile, has extended his contract with Inter Miami until 2028. Should he join the Argentine, Casemiro would have a key role in midfield following the retirement of Sergio Busquets last year.

The franchise, part-owned by another United icon, David Beckham, had initially thought a summer move to be impossible given Casemiro’s huge salary and the MLS’ financial rules.

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo is trying to get his former team-mate to sign for Al-Nassr instead of joining Lionel Messi (Image: Yasser Bakhsh, Getty Images)

Article continues below

But the Brazilian veteran is believed to have enjoyed his recent family holiday to Miami and has reportedly told friends he would like the idea of living there. He would need to make compromises if he wants to play in the MLS, however, while Al-Nassr are capable of offering a more lucrative pay packet.

Casemiro is currently enjoying arguably his best season at United, having scored seven goals and assisted twice in 30 appearances. His impact across his 28 league starts has been tremendous, with Michael Carrick’s side in third place and on the verge of Champions League qualification.

Football.title: Harry Kane has already made his feelings clear on Arsenal stars 'who should be banned'
Football.content:
Harry Kane has already made his feelings clear on Arsenal stars 'who should be banned'

England captain Harry Kane has already laid out how he feels about players leaving the camp early

View 3 Images England captain Harry Kane has already shared his thoughts on players pulling out of camp following a string of recent withdrawals (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

Harry Kane has made it very clear he "doesn't like" England players pulling out of international duty when it isn't entirely necessary. And his previous comments are as important as ever after Gabby Agbonlahor suggested that deserting players "should be banned."

‌



Thomas Tuchel's side host Japan in a friendly on Tuesday, having drawn 1-1 with Uruguay only four days earlier . The manager's squad has been decimated after eight players withdrew from camp to return to their respective clubs, three of whom represent Premier League leaders Arsenal.

‌



Former Tottenham captain Kane addressed player commitment in November 2024, when caretaker coach Lee Carsley had his selection rocked by eight withdrawals prior to a UEFA Nations League clash with Greece.

‌



"I think England comes before anything," Kane told ITV at the time, when asked about what it means to represent the Three Lions. "It comes before club, and it is the most important thing you play as a professional footballer.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Gareth [Southgate] was hot on that, and he wasn't afraid to make decisions if that started to drift from certain players. It's a shame this week, obviously. Yeah, I think it's a tough period of the season and maybe that's been taken advantage of a little bit.

‌



Thomas Tuchel admits mass international withdrawal of Arsenal stars looks 'suspicious' READ MORE :

"I don't really like it if I'm totally honest. I think as I just said there England comes before anything, any club situation. The joy to play for England.

"I think Gareth brought that back. Every camp, people were excited to come, every camp people wanted to play for England and, yeah, that's the most important thing."

Noni Madueke's withdrawal from England camp wasn't seen as suspicious, given the Arsenal winger appeared to suffer a genuine injury against Uruguay. However, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka's exits have been criticised by some fans, given neither player featured in that game.

‌



View 3 Images Questions have been raised over the timing of Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice's returns to Arsenal (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

There's no way of knowing just how severe any injuries or knocks the players might have picked up truly are. However, ex-Aston Villa frontman Agbonlahor didn't pull any punches when questioning the legitimacy of their absences after 10 Arsenal players from different national teams similarly pulled out of international camps this week.

Speaking on talkSPORT, he said: "If I was part of the Premier League and I was making a decision, I would bring in a new rule, you miss the next Premier League game available if you pull out of international duty.

‌



View 3 Images Gabby Agbonlahor suggested players who pull out of international duty should be obliged to miss their next Premier League fixture (Image: talkSPORT)

"I tell you something, players will stop pulling out. Playing for your country is an honour. If I'm Harry Kane, I'm speaking about this and saying, 'Come on, guys, let's not go back to what we were doing four or five years ago, where players are pulling out non-stop.'

"I get it, Arteta is doing everything possible to win these trophies. Their next game after the international break is the FA Cup [quarter-final] against Southampton. I'm just not keen on players pulling out of international duty. It's an honour to play for your country. It doesn't sit right with me."

Jurgen Klopp returned to Liverpool for an LFC Legends match against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, with the former Reds boss given a hero's welcome at Anfield

View 2 Images Former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp returned to Anfield on Saturday (Image: Getty Images)

Jurgen Klopp has expressed his gratitude to Liverpool for the reception he received on his 'homecoming' to Merseyside.

‌



The former Reds manager, forever an iconic figure at Anfield after delivering Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, two League Cups and a Club World Cup glory during nearly nine years at the club, returned to the city for an LFC Legends fixture against another of his former sides, Borussia Dortmund, on Saturday.

‌



Klopp received a hero's welcome as he presided over an entertaining 2-2 draw at Anfield, but on the days surrounding the match he participated in various community initiatives in support of the LFC Foundation, for which he continues to serve as an ambassador having assumed the position following his exit as Reds manager in 2024.

‌



Man Utd given Sandro Tonali encouragement as Newcastle CEO makes transfer admission READ MORE :

Following a whirlwind few days back on Merseyside, Klopp posted to Instagram on Monday evening to share several photographs from his visit, writing: "Thank you to everyone who made my homecoming so special" as he tagged the LFC Foundation.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FC FACEBOOK PAGE! All the latest news and analysis from Anfield on the Liverpool Echo's dedicated LFC Facebook page

Speaking following the match on Saturday, in which Liverpool's goals came from Thiago Alcantara and Jay Spearing, Klopp said: "Enjoyed every second.

‌



"My role was definitely not to have a lot of words. I was here for the Foundation and to be part of a really special experience.

View 2 Images Jurgen Klopp enjoyed his return to Anfield (Image: PETER POWELL / AFP via Getty Images)

"For me, a very special experience after a while – being around, being that close, seeing all the Liverpool lads and then seeing the Dortmund lads as well because that was like 80 per cent of my players.

Football.title: New theory emerges of why Ben White got 'really upset' during England camp
Football.content:
New theory emerges of why Ben White got 'really upset' during England camp

Ben White recently returned to the England squad for the first time since the World Cup 2022 when he exited the camp citing personal reasons

View 2 Images Ben White has returned to the England squad for the first time since 2022 (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

A new theory has emerged surrounding Ben White’s infamous England fallout. The Arsenal defender returned to the Three Lions squad for the first time under Thomas Tuchel this month.

‌



White was called up as an injury replacement for Jarell Quansah. He was jeered by sections of England fans after coming on as a substitute against Uruguay to end his international exile on Friday.

‌



The 28-year-old looked to have scored a late winner for Tuchel’s side before conceding a penalty that ensured the match ended 1-1. However, speculation continues over the cause of his earlier dispute during Gareth Southgate's time in charge.

‌



The Arsenal star left the World Cup squad in 2022 due to personal reasons. While there have been persistent rumours of a row with England's coaching staff, a fresh explanation for his absence has emerged.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“This is what I’m led to understand has happened with Ben White,” broadcaster Adrian Durham said on talkSPORT. “The players were told to watch videos of opponents and they were given videos on their laptops, iPads, whatever it was.

‌



Thomas Tuchel admits mass international withdrawal of Arsenal stars looks 'suspicious' READ MORE :

Inside England's World Cup base with security concerns and scorching heat addressed READ MORE :

“He decided not to and the England analysts knew, because they had the tech, who had and who hadn’t watched the videos. When asked about it, Ben White got really upset about it to the point where he quit England.

“If that is true, why on earth would Thomas Tuchel want him back in the squad when he’s not prepared to put the hard yards in to be as good as he possibly can against the opponents England are up against. If it’s not true, I apologise, but let’s have the flipping truth.”

White was booed at several points during his appearance against Uruguay, including when he was announced as the team’s goalscorer. England boss Tuchel admitted to being disappointed by the crowd’s reaction to the versatile defender.

‌



View 2 Images White scored his first England goal on Friday (Image: Alex Davidson - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

However, he could still start England’s upcoming game against Japan on Tuesday. The Three Lions are set to rotate their team and Tuchel has admitted White is in his plans.

“He has our support and I think he feels our support and the support from the group,” Tuchel said of White being jeered. “I understand that it happened to some other players already and hopefully we got it out of our system and if he plays tomorrow, there's a chance - because it would make sense to play a lot of players who have fresh legs and didn’t start the first match.

Article continues below

“He is one of them – and if he has a good training session he’s in the mix. I’m not involved in all the meetings and talks that go on without the coach and I was in a lot of meetings looking at Japan and stuff. So I am not fully aware but I think so – that’s my guess. He was good, again good in training and good in the group.”

Football.title: Mason Greenwood stance on Jamaica, national team's new comment and squad opinions on him
Football.content:
Mason Greenwood stance on Jamaica, national team's new comment and squad opinions on him

Mason Greenwood is yet to make a decision on his international future, despite reports that he has obtained a Jamaican passport, with some details still needing to be ironed out

View 3 Images Mason Greenwood is yet to make a decision over his international future (Image: Dave Winter/Shutterstock)

Jamaica are one win away from booking their place at this summer's World Cup but whether Mason Greenwood will be watching from afar is still unclear. They will take on DR Congo on Tuesday night (10pm) after overcoming New Caledonia in the semi‑finals.

‌



Much has been made of whether the former Manchester United forward will go on to represent Jamaica, following reports that he obtained his passport last September. There had been anticipation he would join the squad for the first time during the World Cup qualifiers against Trinidad and Tobago and Bermuda.

‌



However, ESPN reported (via Foot Mercato) that he had yet to complete the change‑of‑association form required to represent Jamaica and had not agreed to be called up for those matches.

‌



Thomas Tuchel has made thoughts clear on recalling Mason Greenwood for England READ MORE :

Here, Mirror Football looks at the latest developments surrounding Greenwood and whether there's any real possibility of him playing for the Jamaica national team.

Greenwood's stance

According to Jamaica head coach Rudolph Speid, Greenwood is yet to decide on his international future.

Jamaica president comments

Last November, Jamaican FA president Michael Ricketts said the federation hoped to have him available for the 2026 World Cup playoff campaign. But months later, nothing has changed.

‌



"Initially, he seemed delighted that his paperwork was finally in order," Ricketts said. "When we sent it to him and I asked for his opinion, he told me it was a family decision not to make himself available at the moment."

'Expected him to join'

Former Jamaica head coach Steve McCLaren admitted they expected Greenwood to join the national team back in September. "We acquired a passport and we expected him to be coming to this camp but in a conversation with his family, he's not going to commit at this time to anybody," he said at the time.

View 3 Images Steve McClaren said they had expected Greenwood to join Jamaica back in September (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"He's taking his time over that, so it's a little bit disappointing. We probably have to be more patient, but we will keep the contact, we will keep pursuing him because I know from my conversations with Mason and his family that he loves Jamaica, respects Jamaica.

"He wants to concentrate on club football and not commit to an international team at the present moment. We have to respect that however much we've worked hard to get him here for these camps. So, who knows in the future."

Senior players' 'disagreement'

Former Newcastle United midfielder Isaac Hayden said he 'can’t see why' Greenwood or any player who skipped earlier qualifiers, should now be allowed to join the national team.

‌



"I've only played for Jamaica for a year, and there was some resistance to me when I started, but I have played 12 games and everyone can see my passion and the way I play the game," Hayden said. "I give everything on the pitch, and I wanted to be there to help Jamaica progress to the World Cup.

View 3 Images Isaac Hayden has made his feelings clear about Greenwood potentially joining the Jamaica national team (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"They want to have the best team on the pitch, but I said it to the JFF: 'If a player is not willing to commit for the last round of qualifying, unless they're injured, I do not see why they should be joining the group in March or at the end of the season if we qualify.' There is no way that should be allowed to happen."

Hayden went on to argue that Greenwood's late inclusion would undermine the team's integrity. "The quality of the player, his numbers, what he is producing, is of the highest level," he admitted.

"But it comes down to principle and integrity. If players can just rock up because of a World Cup, it would make the whole thing a farce. That would say a lot about the player, and the organisation for allowing that to happen."

‌



Defender Amari'i Bell echoed Hayden's concerns, adding: "Many of us for years have put our blood, sweat and tears into playing for the nation, with a lot of things happening in the background. We've had to deal with all that.

"It wouldn't seem fair to people who have been through that whole process and will never get another chance to play at a World Cup. It's a bit controversial."

He also added that the squad would need a group discussion before any new player came in. "Definitely, especially when it's a World Cup," he stated. "You want good vibes and good energy around the squad.

‌



"You wouldn't want any distance between any players."

Ex-player 'welcomes' return

Meanwhile, former Jamaica international Frank Sinclair would like to see Greenwood represent the Reggae Boyz. He said: "I myself was in a situation where I decided to play for Jamaica when they qualified for the 1998 World Cup. That's when I was asked to play. I hadn't been asked to play during the qualifiers and in the end, Jamaica will make a decision that will allow them, if they qualify for the World Cup, to give their best.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



"They might have the opportunity to recruit him once they get there, but they still have a lot of work to do to get there. From a purely footballing perspective, the answer is obvious: yes, absolutely [Jamaica needs Greenwood back]. His footballing qualities would significantly strengthen the Jamaican team. But it goes beyond that. Many people don't share the same opinion about him as a person.

"It all depends on what Jamaica wants to do to create a culture within the national team. It's a difficult question. From a purely footballing perspective, yes, of course, you want Mason Greenwood on your team. At the same time, there are things in the world that are more important than football, and it's a difficult question to answer. The nation, the players, and the staff would have to accept and support him 100%, because many people will try to sabotage him.

‌



"It's not simply a matter of dual nationality; you can now play for Jamaica. Representing Jamaica involves much more than that."

'Obsessed with representing England again'

Mirror Football previously reported that the player was 'obsessed' with representing England again but Thomas Tuchel confirmed in September that the player isn't in his thoughts.

At the time, the head coach said: "I have not spoken to him until now. I have not spoken to him or his camp. My understanding was that he tries to play for Jamaica so we didn't give it another thought. He was not in the mix at the moment and he is not in our thoughts for our team."

Football.title: Peters ready for 250th game between Hull KR vs Hull FC: 'This is the biggest derby'
Football.content:
Hull KR head coach Willie Peters has been involved in many a derby match throughout his playing and coaching career, but he says none come close to that between the Robins and Hull FC.

The Good Friday meeting between Hull KR and Hull FC, live on Sky Sports, will mark the 250th time that the two Hull clubs will have locked horns.

You have to go all the way back to 1899 to find the first fixture between east and west Hull. It was on Hull KR's home turf, as this one is, and the Robins took the victory.

If you look at the stats in just Super League, there have been 50 meetings of the two teams so far. Hull KR have won 26 of them, while Hull FC have prevailed in 24.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Sky Sports' The Bench podcast with Jenna Brooks, Hull KR's Jez and Hull FC's Davy Litten discuss who their family support when the cousins face each other

The question always rages about which derby is the biggest. Fans will strongly defend their rivalry as the greatest in the sport or even the biggest in the world.

Peters has been involved is some iconic clashes throughout his career on both sides of the world. He has experienced St Helens vs Wigan as a player, the Sydney clash, and St George up against Cronulla.

Having been a part of all those rivalries, Peters stands firm in his belief that the Hull derby is the biggest of them all and there is no bigger week to back that conviction than ahead of their 250th meeting.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Betfred Super League match between Hull KR and St Helens

"Derby week is huge. It is the 250th derby and we know what we are going to get, they know what they are going to get," Peters said.

"It is going to be an electric atmosphere here. There is no bigger derby.

"I have been in some massive derbies, involved in huge derbies over the years.

"I was at Wigan playing at Saints. I was at the Rabbitohs against the Roosters. I was at St George against Cronulla. This is the biggest.

"No matter where you sit on the table, regardless of where we sit, it is always a tasty game and it is always an enjoyable week.

"I am really looking forward to it."

Football.title: England women's head coach Edwards on shortlist for new T20 Hall of Fame
Football.content:
England women's head coach Charlotte Edwards is amongst the names on a shortlist for the T20 Hall of Fame presented by Vitality, celebrating the icons of domestic T20 cricket in England and Wales.

As part of the launch, six men and six women have been shortlisted to become the first-ever inductees.

An independent expert panel - comprising former players, commentators and journalists - will select the first two men, and two women, from the shortlisted names to be inducted.

Fans will also get the opportunity to have their say via a Public Vote, which will form a weighted element of the final decision making process.

The inaugural inductees will be revealed on 15 May, ahead of the opening night of the 2026 Vitality Blast on Friday 22 May.

Men's shortlisted players: Ravi Bopara, Danny Briggs, Joe Denly, Samit Patel, James Vince, Luke Wright.

Ravi Bopara, Danny Briggs, Joe Denly, Samit Patel, James Vince, Luke Wright. Women's shortlisted players: Charlotte Edwards, Kirstie Gordon, Heather Knight, Katie Levick, Nat Sciver-Brunt, Danni Wyatt-Hodge.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Somerset lift the Vitality Blast trophy after a thrilling win over Hampshire

Samit Patel, who has played in every season of the Vitality Blast men's competition since its inception in 2003, said: "To be shortlisted for the T20 Hall of Fame is something that I'm hugely proud of especially alongside some great names.

"It means a lot to be recognised for what I've tried to give to the domestic game over so many years. To be one of the first players inducted would be an incredible honour and something I'd feel very privileged to be part of."

Danni Wyatt-Hodge, who is a three-time domestic T20 winner and the leading run scorer since the KSL began in 2016, said: "I was absolutely delighted when I found out and I told my family straight away. To be shortlisted alongside great players is an honour and it would be amazing to be inducted into the Hall of Fame - it's a big deal!

"It's the first time I have been nominated for anything like this so hopefully I can be one of the inducted players. I'm incredibly proud."

2026 short-listed player

Women

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Grace Harris dominant 63 not out helped Surrey beat Warwickshire Bears to become inaugural Vitality Blast women's champions!

Edwards was captain of 2016 Kia Super League winners Southern Vipers and led them to final in 2017 before her retirement.

Gordon has the second most wickets in women's domestic T20s during qualifying period - 75 wickets at an average 16.6. She is a two-time leading wicket-taker in a season - (2018 KSL and 2024 CEC) and three-time top-five wicket-taker in a season.

Knight is a two-time KSL winning captain with Western Storm and player of the match in 2019 final with an unbeaten 78 from 53 balls.

She has been a top-five run scorer in a season four times.

Levick has the most wickets in women's domestic T20 cricket during qualifying period - 85 at 17.2.

She has been top-five wicket taker in a season three times.

Sciver-Brunt was a KSL-winning captain in 2018 when she scored the third most runs in the competition that season; 11th most domestic T20 runs during qualifying period - 1,211 at 43.25; 38 wickets during qualifying period at 24.7.

She has been a top-five run scorer in a season three times.

Wyatt-Hodge is a three-time champion - 2025 Vitality Blast winner and Charlotte Edwards Cup (2022 and 2023).

A leading run scorer in all T20 competitions during qualifying period - 1,710 at 33.5 (300 runs ahead of next best).

Two-time most runs in a season (2019 and 2023) and four times in the top-five for most runs in a season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mikey Jones' huge six smashed the back window of a car during Lancashire Lightning’s T20 blast match against Durham County. X Credit: @lancscricket

Men

Image: Ravi Bopara is also on the shortlist

Bopara, a 2019 title winner with Essex, has played in 236 men's domestic T20 matches and is one of only two players to feature inside the all-time top-10 for both wicket-takers and run scorers in the competition.

He has the third most runs in the men's competition - 5,290 at 29.1 - and eighth most wickets - 169 wickets at 26.3.

Briggs, a 2010 and 2012 title winner with Hampshire, has taken the most wickets in history of the domestic men's T20 competition - 268 wickets at 20.5.

Four times he has been a top-three wicket taker in a season and he is equal second-most 4+ wickets in a match.

Denly, a two-time title winner with Kent in 2007 and 2021 has the second most runs in history of the men's domestic T20 competition - 5,554 at 28.8.

He is a two-time leading run scorer in a season (2008 and 2017), and the first men's player to score a century and take a hat-trick in the same T20 match - in front of a full house away to Surrey in 2018.

Vince, a three-time title winner with Hampshire - 2022 as captain and also 2010 and 2012, hold the record for most runs in history of the men's domestic T20 competition - 6,357 at 35.7.

He has hit the most half-centuries (46) and second-equal most centuries (5) as well as most catches in history of men's T20 competition (135). Three-time most runs in a season (2015, 2022, 2023) and five times he has been in the top-five run scorers in a season (2015, 2017, 2022, 2023, 2025).

Football.title: Williamson, Mead and 17-year-old Parkinson included in latest England squad
Football.content:
Leah Williamson and Beth Mead have been included in the latest England squad ahead of World Cup Qualifiers against Spain and Iceland, while 17-year-old Erica Meg Parkinson has received a first senior call-up.

Mead missed out on the February camp due to injury, while Lionesses captain Williamson is being given time to prove her own fitness.

She has been dealing with a hamstring injury that has kept her out of Arsenal's last three matches, but with two weeks until the first match of the international break against Spain, Williamson has been called up.

When asked if she would be ready for the game at Wembley, Wiegman said: "We're expecting that. Leah had an injury after the Euros, then she's coming back. She had some small setbacks but overall, she's doing well.

"When she's playing, she's playing really well. We have been careful with her, and have Arsenal, and she is on that too. I think she's going to make it so that's why we put her in the squad."

Image: Leah Williamson has been called up for the latest England camp

Uncapped 17-year-old Parkinson also receives her first senior call-up, having come through England's youth pathways.

Born in Singapore to an English father and Japanese mother, she plays for Portuguese first division side Valadares Gaia. She is eligible to play for England, Japan, Portugal and Singapore.

"She was surprised," Wiegman said. "She was speechless, she said, but she was very happy and excited.

"We called her up because we're a little bit low in depth in midfield, with injuries to Ella [Toone] and Grace [Clinton], then we look at who's next.

"What we looked at now is the quality she brings and what she's done for club and country and what we needed in the squad.

"We need an attacking midfielder and she came up. Other things come later on, but first of all, we look at what does she show on the pitch. It's a big step to go from U23s and the Portuguese league to our senior level, but she gets the opportunity to show where she stands.

Image: Beth Mead has been recalled after missing out in February due to injury

"She's ready to come in. For every young player that comes into our environment for the first time, of course there is some anxiety. It's a team that has played at such a high level so for every team, it's a step up.

"We're not going to force anything, she's going to show [herself] and hopefully she's going to enjoy it. I don't expect her to get into the starting line-up straight away.

"It's a learning thing for her, but I do hope she can adapt quickly to the level that's needed in the senior environment."

However, Aggie Beever-Jones, Grace Clinton and Ella Toone have not been called up for the April matches due to injury.

The Lionesses face Spain for the first time since the Euro 2025 final on April 14, before travelling to Reykjavik to take on Iceland on April 18.

England are currently top of Group A3 on goal difference ahead of Spain. Only the top spot automatically qualifies for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil.

Who is 17-year-old Parkinson?

It has been quite the whirlwind few months for Parkinson. It was only in December that she was called up for England's U23s at the age of just 17.

In 2024, she was part of the team that reached the final of the U17 Euros and the semi-final of the U17 World Cup. Last summer, she played at the U19 Euros under Lauren Smith.

Wiegman said of the teenager: "She's a dynamic, attacking midfielder, she wants to go forward. She's also very aggressive and pretty technical."

Parkinson also contributes with her fair share of goals too, coupled with the ability to make a good run. She can also play on the wing if needed, giving Wiegman options.

Parkinson and her family moved to Portugal from Singapore when her brother - who has played for Japan at youth level - was scouted to play for Porto's academy.

Speaking to the FA, she said: "We kind of moved because of that but also because of the family - we wanted to be closer to Europe. There's more of a football culture and it's also close to the UK and my dad's family is here. It was for numerous reasons but mainly for football."

The midfielder signed her first professional contract with Valadares Gaia in May 2024, and has played with the likes of Michelle Ageymang and Katie Reid at youth level - both who have recently been called up to Wiegman's senior squad.

But what made Parkinson chose England over Portugal, Japan on Singapore?

Speaking to Girls on the Ball, she said: "They were the first country that came up to me and invited me to start with the NTCs.

"Once I was here and I started going through the pathway, I really liked the culture. All the players that you come across are very kind but they're also very ambitious.

"I really enjoyed the way that England conducted themselves - the training, the games, how we want to play and I related to that."

When asked whether the range of options for Parkinson to play for has any bearing on her call-up, Wiegman replied: "It's up to the player who she wants to play for. What we looked at was what does she show on the pitch."

We may not see her in action during this international break - even the England boss said it was be a 'surprise' if the 17-year-old made an appearance against Spain, who have one of the best midfields in the world. Iceland is the more realistic prospect.

But Wiegman also added she likes surprises, and we have seen teenagers do so for England in the not-too-distant past.

Parkinson has a bright future ahead of her, and could be a Lionesses for the better part of the next 20 years. This camp will be a good learning curve for her, and a marker of where she is at and what more she has to do to reach the same level.

There are also youth tournaments coming up later this year that she will surely be a part of. Keep an eye on the name though - it's one for the future.
