Football.title: Manchester United told 6ft 4in defender is perfect for them – he is one of the best in Europe
Football.content:
Manchester United should be 'all over' Evan Ndicka this summer - he would suit the Premier League perfectly.

That is the view of European football broadcaster Andy Brassell, who has labelled the Roma defender as among the very best in his position in Europe.

5 Ndicka has proved a real bargain after joining Roma on a free transfer in 2023 Credit: Getty

After a resurgence under interim boss Michael Carrick, United look to be closing in on Champions League qualification.

The Red Devils are currently third in the Premier League, six points clear of Chelsea in sixth, with fifth place the cut-off point for making Europe's premier competition as it stands via the European Performance Spots.

With European football promising a much busier fixture calendar next season, United will need to bolster their ranks if they are to compete on all fronts.

Among the areas where they will look to strengthen is central defence, having been found thin on the ground at times this term.

Both Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt have missed significant periods through injury, leaving Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro as the default pairing.

'He'll get even better'

European football journalist Brassell believes Roma defender Ndicka is just the man to take United's defence to the next level.

Since joining Roma in 2023, the Ivorian has carved out a strong reputation, and was named in the 2024/25 Serie A Team of the Season.

This term, the 26-year-old has played in 35 matches altogether, chalking up five goals for a Roma team pushing for a Champions League spot.

Hailing him, Brassell told talkSPORT: “I think he's one of the very best central defenders in Europe and I don't think he's ever really given credit for it."

Pointing out United's recent revival under Carrick, Brassell urged them to capitalise on this by adding Ndicka to their ranks.

5 Highly-rated Ndicka has contributed to eight clean sheets for Roma this season Credit: Getty

5 Brassell has tipped United to sign a strong defender to join the likes of Harry Maguire Credit: Getty

He continued: “If I was a Premier League club, I would be all over Roma for Evan Ndicka. I think he's already a great defender and I think he'll get even better.

“I think the situation where United are at the moment, if they get themselves into the Champions League, it's been a great back end of the season for them under Michael Carrick.

“But they can't allow what's happened over the last couple of months and the positive uptick, in the context of, what I have to say quality-wise is quite an average Premier League this season [take their foot off the gas].

“They've got to really grasp that opportunity and they can't be fooled into thinking that everything's fine.

“They have to go out and make some good signings. And in terms of refreshing that defence, I think Ndicka would be absolutely perfect.”

Brassell pointed out that a move for Ndicka would suit both parties, with Roma likely to have to sell after being sanctioned by UEFA last summer for breaching Financial Fair Play rules.

5 Ndicka first became a wanted man during his five-year stint at Eintracht Frankfurt Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Outlining the logistics of a move, he explained: “You look at him, you look at his age, you look at the fact that Roma are still kind of skint because they've got to abide by the terms of this financial settlement with UEFA, which means that they will have to sell at least one in the summer, you would think.”

Special One-approved

Born in Paris, Ndicka came through the ranks at Auxerre before being snapped up by Eintracht Frankfurt in a £4.5million move in 2018.

He quickly established himself in the Bundesliga, before going on to make 134 appearances over five years in Germany.

Named in the league's Team of the Season in 2022, Ndicka was heavily linked with a move to the Premier League, but opted instead to join former United boss Jose Mourinho at Roma.

And Brassell has hailed 'The Special One' for developing the Parisian from a ball-playing centre-back into the complete defender.

On his progress, Brassell remarked: "You go back to Ndicka and when he was at track Frankfurt you thought, ‘OK this guy could develop into something really good.'

5 Mourinho was Roma manager between 2021 and 2023 and took Ndika under his wing Credit: Getty

“But it's turned out that Roma has been the absolute perfect move for him.

On Mourinho's influence, he continued: “Mourinho did a really good first job with Ndicka.

“It was interesting when he spoke about how he had a promising, but not red-hot start at Roma. Mourinho said, 'Evan is very good on the ball, but he needs to learn that being a defender is actually about defending.'

On this, Brassell added: “Those words, it feels, have really stayed with Ndicka.

"He was always like very, very tidy on the ball, very elegant in the way he moves but now he seems to really relish the defending part of being a defender.

“Actually it's helped him in other ways - he's someone who's more of a danger from attacking set pieces. He gets goals because he's able to be aggressive in the opposition penalty boxes as well."

Football.title: New Arsene Wenger offside rule could soon be rolled out after Canada test
Football.content:
New Arsene Wenger offside rule could soon be rolled out after Canada test

Arsene Wenger’s proposal of a revamped offside ruling will be trialled for the first time in professional football.

The Canadian Premier League (CPL) will become the first competition to launch an official policy of the revised law during the 2026 season.

3 Arsene Wenger's new offside initiative is set for its first-ever pilot Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The legendary Arsenal boss who now stands as FIFA Chief of Global Football Development has been a vocal critic of the current offside procedure.



Why does Wenger want to change the offside rule?

Wenger put forward a revised interpretation aimed at boosting attacking play and favouring more goal scoring situations.

There has been widespread frustration across the sport over what constitutes offside, with some players penalised for the most minimal circumstances.

However, the trial has been given the green light by the International Football Association Board and will start in the Canadian Premier League from April 4.

The CPL confirmed on Thursday that under the new approach an attacking player will be ⁠ruled offside only if there is clear gap, or “daylight”, ​between the attacker and the defender.



That means the attacker will be ​considered onside if any part of the body that can legally score is level with or behind the second-to-last defender.

Reacting to the news, Wenger said: “This is an important pilot.

“By testing this new interpretation in a professional competition, ​we can better understand its impact, including in terms of improving clarity ‌and ⁠the flow of the game and promoting attacking play.



“We look forward to analysing the results of the trial phase.

“We thank the Canadian Premier League and the Canadian Soccer Association for their willingness to support FIFA with this pilot and for providing their competition.”

3 Marginal offsides could soon be a thing of the past in football Credit: Sky Sports



The CPL trial will be conducted in conjunction with FIFA.

World football’s governing body will oversee the research and evaluation framework while working alongside Canada Soccer to prepare ⁠match officials, players and clubs.

James Johnson, commissioner of the Canadian Premier League and group CEO of Canadian Soccer Media & Entertainment said: “This is about positioning the Canadian Premier League at the forefront of ​innovation and contributing meaningfully to the global evolution ​of ⁠the game."

What other changes will be rolled out?

The CPL also confirmed that it will be introducing FIFA-designed and IFAB-approved procedures including Football Video Support to combat at time-wasting and improving match ​efficiency.

FVS will see coaches given a set number of challenges per game to be used in match-changing incidents on goals, penalties, red cards and mistaken identity.

The coach is required to give a request card to the fourth official before the match restarts.



3 Wenger's proposed offside rule change has not gone down well with fans Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The fourth official will also check for any offences in the lead up to goals, but will not replace VAR.

FIFA say the measures are being brought in to ‘enhance match tempo and reduce time-wasting were approved and updates were given on ongoing developments in offside-related technologies and trials.’

Football.title: Viktor Gyokeres boosted by teammates’ vow on boss who never played him in Premier League
Football.content:
Viktor Gyokeres boosted by teammates’ vow on boss who never played him in Premier League

Viktor Gyokeres has found the form to put Sweden on the cusp of World Cup qualification - but that's no surprise to Jesper Karlstrom.

The Arsenal striker fired his nation into the playoff final against Poland with a stunning hat-trick to down Ukraine 3-1.

5 Karlstrom (right) was just waiting for the goals to flow for Gyokeres Credit: Getty

Gyokeres' treble took his total for the season to 19 goals for club and country, with 11 of his strikes coming in the Premier League.

The 27-year-old has enjoyed a remarkable start to 2026, having initially struggled to settle following his £55million move to Arsenal.

Gyokeres 'will just go until it works'

Gyokeres scored just two Premier League goals from September 13 until the end of January, but has since enjoyed a flurry of form.

And his Sweden teammate Karlstrom predicted as much in an interview with talkSPORT during Udinese’s media day event.

"It's really nice to see him [perform like this]," the Serie A club's captain said earlier this month.

"But I think in the national team, he always performed good.

"So even though he struggled a little bit in the beginning, I wasn't that worried.

"For him, I know him really good and what kind of person he is. He will just go until it works. We all know his qualities.

"But it's really nice to see that he will come into this camp with confidence."

5 The Swede has netted three in his last four league games for Arsenal Credit: Getty

5 Sweden now face Poland for a place in the World Cup Credit: Getty

Gyokeres teammate knew goals 'would come'

Gyokeres may have been worried about reuniting with Graham Potter, who did not give him a single minute of Premier League action when the pair were at Brighton together.

Injury ruled him out of the Englishman's first two games in charge of Sweden in November, meaning he has to wait for his chance.

But a hat-trick against Ukraine more than silenced the doubters, and Karlstrom was already predicting Gyokeres to explode in front of goal.

"You can ask Keinan Davis how good I spoke about it," he added to talkSPORT. "I knew the goals, they would come."

Karlstrom knows a thing or two about playing with elite Sweden strikers, having shared a dressing room with Zlatan Ibrahimovic.

5 Karlstrom has also ranked this Sweden side at the very top Credit: AFP

5 Kallstrom had more than enough World Cup and Champions League experience to make the deal worth while Credit: Getty

That connection was particularly special to the Udinese skipper, who grew up with a poster of the ex-Manchester United star on his wall.

Karlstrom admitted he never told Ibrahimović that fact, and instead attempted to play it cool when on Sweden duty together.

"I didn't want to be going after him all the time, trying to be his friend," he told talkSPORT.com.

"It was amazing to play with him, to see him this close on the pitch. When we spoke a few times, he probably has a lot of people coming after him and just trying to be his friend.

"I tried to… not that he had to come big with me but just in a natural way." Play it cool? "Yeah, a little bit like that."

Football.title: Football news LIVE: De Zerbi to Tottenham talks still ongoing, Newcastle chief addresses Howe future, Cucurella defends Rosenior
Football.content:
By VAR and away...

A survey run by the Football Supporters' Association says around 75 per cent of fans are against VAR.

Close to 8,000 fans took part in the poll, with just over half of them attending more than 15 home games each season.

More than 97 per cent of respondents disagree with the statement that VAR makes football more enjoyable to watch.

The idea that VAR has made the match-going experience better was opposed by more than 90 per cent.

In fact, 75.71 per cent of respondents say they do not support the use of VAR in football.

More than 70 per cent disagree that VAR has improved the overall accuracy of decisions made by referees.

Less than three per cent agree that VAR decisions are reached in a reasonable amount of time.

The majority do not believe they are now being made more quickly, despite efforts being made to speed up the process.

As well as this, more than 90 per cent feel the technology has removed the spontaneous joy of goal celebrations.

A Premier League spokesperson said: "The Premier League recognises the importance of minimising the impact of VAR on the supporter experience. Since the introduction of the VAR Improvement Plan at the start of the 2024/25 season, the League and PGMO have implemented in‑stadium referee announcements and more proactive communications, while there has also been the introduction of semi‑automated offside technology – all designed to improve clarity, speed, and communication around key decisions.

"VAR delivers more correct decisions. In recent seasons, there have been around 100 correct VAR overturns per season – instances where goals would otherwise have been incorrectly awarded or disallowed, or red cards or penalties missed or wrongly given.

"The Premier League works closely with PGMO to continually improve the operation of VAR, with the aim of ensuring minimal interference in matches wherever possible. The League applies a high threshold for VAR intervention, with the Referee’s Call taking precedence. As a result, VAR is less intrusive in the Premier League than in other European leagues, including the Champions League, where VAR intervenes almost twice as often.

"As part of ongoing dialogue with supporters, Premier League research indicates fans are largely in favour of keeping VAR, but improving the way it is used.

"This remains a priority for both the Premier League and PGMO, and the League will continue to engage with all stakeholders to build on the progress made through the VAR Improvement Plan."

Football.title: Serie A star makes vow about ‘friend’ Antoine Semenyo and moment Morgan Rogers clicked
Football.content:
Antoine Semenyo is smashing it - but I hope I can come up against him one day and keep him quiet.

That is the verdict of Udinese star Jordan Zemura, who was one of many alumni of a bygone Bournemouth era to be thriving in Europe.

5 Zemura [left] was part of the most star studded team in Bournemouth's recent history Credit: Getty

The 26-year-old was part of the Cherries' promotion-winning side in 2021/22 that secured the club's return to the Premier League.



Zemura spent the majority of that campaign wrestling with then-Leeds United loanee Leif Davis for gametime at left-back.

The Zimbabwe international ultimately won the battle and continued with Bournemouth in the top-flight, while Davis joined Ipswich Town.

However, Zemura - who has since spent the past three years in Italy's Serie A - was keen to credit his ex-teammate for his development.

"Great player," he said of Davis during Udinese's international media days event. "There's a lot of things that I picked up from him.



"He probably doesn't even know it to be fair. But we were competing against each other.

"Without him being there, I definitely wouldn't have had that competition to be where I am now.



"He came from Leeds, so obviously, not like he was always going to make it. But his talent was always there.

"So I guess it was just manager's preference at the end of the day. But, there's so much stuff that me and him... just some training and seeing the way he does certain things and stuff like that."



Zemura started in all but one of his 33 Championship appearances in the 2021/22 season, forming such a strong partnership on the left flank with Jaidon Anthony that a young Morgan Rogers struggled to get a look in.

5 The defender has one assist in 15 Serie A appearances this season Credit: Getty

5 Zemura remains highly regarded on the south coast following his exploits in Bournemouth's promotion-winning season Credit: Getty

Rogers has 'crazy catalogue of finishing'

The now-Aston Villa superstar arrived at the Vitality Stadium on the second of his three loans away from Manchester City in August 2021.

However, Rogers was sent back to the Etihad at the midway point of the season after making just one Championship start.



"He was young, though", Zemura added, defending the 12-cap England international.

"Morgan, at the time, was like 19, but finishing was unbelievable, like left foot, right foot.

"I always used to say that he's got like a crazy catalogue of finishing, in terms of either smashing it or finessing it.

"But as soon as it clicked, like I just knew that, yeah, 'You're going to do well for yourself, man!'"

5 Zemura claimed Rogers' 'unbelievable finishing' was evident as a teenager



5 Zemura played alongside Semenyo in his final Premier League appearance for the Cherries Credit: Getty

Semenyo is 'smashing it'

The following season, Zemura made 19 Premier League appearances, but a contract dispute meant he was made to train with the under-21s and didn't feature at all after a 3-2 defeat to Arsenal in March.

His final partner down the left in a Bournemouth shirt was Semenyo, who has since made Champions League history after completing a £62.5million move to Man City in January.

"Even Ants, I've known him since we were younger," Zemura continued to talkSPORT. "Just played against each other when he was young, like 18, 17. He was at Bristol City.

"And he's not far from where I live, so yeah, that's my good friend, man."



On Semenyo’s Man City move: "Oh, smashing it, absolutely. So I hope I can come up against him one day and then try to keep him quiet."

News.title: Eleven men in court charged over death of DIY SOS dad – 11 years after he was ‘kicked like a football’ following match
News.content:
IN THE DOCK Eleven men in court charged over death of DIY SOS dad – 11 years after he was ‘kicked like a football’ following match

ELEVEN men have appeared in court charged over the death of a dad who appeared on DIY SOS – 11 years after he was attacked following a match.

Simon Dobbin was allegedly “kicked like a football” after going to watch his beloved Cambridge United play Southend United in March 2015.





The 48-year-old was left with permanent brain damage and unable to walk or talk following the 90-second assault.

Dad-of-three Simon passed away in October 2020.

The 11 men – aged from 29 to 49 and all from Essex – sat side-by-side in the dock when they appeared at Colchester Magistrates Court today.

They are each charged with manslaughter on October 21, 2020 – the date that Simon died aged 48.



The defendants are Greg Allen, 37, Jamie Chambers, 33, Lewis Courtnell, 43, and Philip McGill, 40.

Scott Nicholls, 49, Matthew Petchey, 35, Rhys Pullen, 29, Thomas Randall, 31, Michael Shawyer, 40, Alexander Woods, 33, James Woods, 33, have also been also charged.

They were all granted unconditional bail ahead of a hearing at Basildon Crown Court on May 1.

A twelfth man, Ryan Carter, 40, is set to appear in front of magistrates later today also accused of manslaughter.



Simon was allegedly attacked following a fight earlier in the day which he had no involvement in.

A small group of Cambridge United supporters were targeted and during the horror, Simon was kicked and stamped on repeatedly, it is understood.

In 2017, Simon and his family touched the nation’s on BBC show DIY SOS as a team of volunteers transformed his home to help meet his needs.

His wife Nicole tragically revealed he had died in a moving tribute.

She said: “I lost my gentle giant, words cannot express the loss I’m feeling.



“I’m thankful for the fantastic memories I have, he fought so very hard to be with his family.

“Sadly his heart wasn’t strong enough, but he is now at peace and will be forever in my heart.”

Detective Superintendent Stephen Jennings said previously: “This is a significant milestone in an extremely complex investigation, and comes as the result of the professionalism, dedication, and hard work from a team of highly skilled officers and staff.

“Investigations such as these are challenging and can take time, it has required hundreds of hours of painstaking work to get to this stage.

“Throughout this time we have worked closely with the Crown Prosecution Service.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Simon’s case is one that has evoked a great deal of emotion, but I would ask people to be mindful about commentary to ensure those charged are able to have a fair trial.

“I want to thank Simon’s family – his wife Nicole and daughter Emily – for their patience and unwavering support for our team.”

News.title: Top questions parents ask the internet about their kids revealed, including why they ‘hate vegetables’ & ‘sit in boxes’
News.content:
THE quirky questions parents have asked the internet about their kids include “how common is it for children to get stuck in a washing machine?” and “why do kids like sitting in a box?”.

Search engine analysis revealed some of the bizarre queries parents have fielded as they look to better understand how their kids see the world – including the likes of “why do kids draw dogs all the same?”.





“Do kids naturally hate vegetables?” was also asked 38 times over an average month, while “Why do kids say ‘are we nearly there yet’?’’ was also typed into a search bar 32 times.

“Do kids write diaries without being told to?” and “why do kids fold their ears?” are also among some of the random questions that have been asked of the internet.

It comes after Specsavers research of 1,000 parents of children aged five to seven found 88 per cent use traditional search engines to try to understand their kids better – an average of five times per week.

More than four in 10 (41 per cent) asked questions about their child’s habits or routines, such as sleep or repetitive behaviours, while 39 per cent questioned whether certain behaviours are common.



Specific interests (29 per cent), such as items they are drawn to, was also a common theme, after 90 per cent of parents said their children were drawn to ‘mundane’ items, such as rocks (31 per cent), cardboard boxes (31 per cent), puddles (29 per cent), and leaves (28 per cent).

“Is it normal for my child….” was the opening to a search for 54 per cent of parents.

The research also found 39 per cent have searched for answers online about their little one’s physical health.

The most common themes included rashes or skin conditions (49 per cent), high temperatures (44 per cent), or developmental milestones (38 per cent).



But only 17 per cent have ever sought advice about their vision or eye health.

Child psychologist, Dr Elizabeth Kilbey, who is working with Specsavers, said: “It’s not surprising parents are turning to search engines to help navigate the many questions that come with raising children – from behaviour and development to the often weird and wonderful things kids say or do.

20 QUIRKY SEARCH TERMS ASKED BY PARENTS Why are kids saying 6 7? Do kids naturally hate vegetables? Why do kids like sitting in a box? Why do kids love cardboard boxes so much? Why do kids say are we nearly there yet? Why do kids fold their ears? How common is it for children to get stuck in a washing machine? Do kids write diaries without being told to? Why do kids draw dogs all the same? Why are kids talking in letters these days? Why do kids like food in shapes? Why are kids throwing popcorn at chicken jockey? Why do kids act like cats? Do kids poke each other’s bum? How come most kids just instinctively make potions in the bathroom? Why do kids cheer during fire alarm? Do kids like to watch the water tornado in the bath? Why do kids draw loads of fingers on hands? Why do kids eat sponges? Why are kids mewing?

“Children are curious and imaginative, and this plays a vital role in how they learn, explore and build confidence.

“Because so much of that discovery is visual, clear vision is crucial to their development.

“In all areas of life, and the classroom especially, clear vision is fundamental.



“Being able to see and focus underpins learning – when vision is affected, it can influence a child’s attention, engagement and behaviour.

“That’s why parents should prioritise eye health as an important part of their child’s overall wellbeing.”

The study found a higher percentage of parents prefer to use online tools to ask such queries (35 per cent) versus turning to someone in their lives (17 per cent).

This preference was put down to getting immediate answers (47 per cent), having a range of information to compare (41 per cent), and the fact it is often much quicker (33 per cent).

But 18 per cent do this out of a worry they would be judged for wondering these things about their child, while 21 per cent think they can get a more objective answer from strangers.



But eye health does not seem to be one of the topics parents ask either other people or the internet about – of those who hadn’t ever searched anything to do with this topic, 10 per cent thought their child was too young for it to be a worry and 11 per cent assumed their school would flag any concerns.

It also emerged 13 per cent were unaware of any common eyesight issues which can affect children, such as short-sightedness or lazy eye (amblyopia).

Worryingly, 15 per cent of those polled had never taken their child for an eye test, while 11 per cent had not done so within the last two years, according to the OnePoll.com data.

The main reason for this was simply because their child had not complained about their vision (21 per cent), with 12 per cent saying they would make an appointment if there appeared to be an issue.

Dr Nigel Best, optometrist from Specsavers, added: “This research proves how easy it is to overlook a child’s eye health unless obvious symptoms appear.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But that’s why being proactive is so important. Regular eye tests can identify issues early – often before a child realises anything is wrong.

“What many parents may not realise is that many sight conditions, such as myopia in kids, can be managed or corrected if they’re detected before the age of eight, while vision is still developing.”

News.title: Vile Uber Eats driver who returned to customer’s address and raped her in twisted sex attack jailed
News.content:
SICK ATTACK Vile Uber Eats driver who returned to customer’s address and raped her in twisted sex attack jailed

AN UBER Eats delivery driver who raped a vulnerable customer after returning to her home has been jailed.

Jitendrakumar Prajapati, 47, delivered lunch to his victim in Boston, Lincolnshire, as the pair struck up a conversation – before he launched a sickening attack just hours later.



The twisted delivery driver told the woman he had just moved to the area and didn’t know anyone.

He asked her for help getting a visa and with work before asking the victim for her Instagram account.



They went on to swap phone numbers after Prajapati asked if he could stay in touch.

The delivery driver left the victim’s property before he returned at around 5pm the same day.

Prajapati and the woman again engaged in small talk before things took a sinister turn and the twisted delivery driver raped her.

In a frantic bid to cover up the vile act Prajapati messaged her after leaving her home to say: “Hey I am sorry.”



He then changed his WhatsApp username and enabled “disappearing chat”.

The two would go on to exchange a number of messages in the following hours with the victim accusing the delivery driver of sexual assault.

Prajapati was apologetic as he desperately begged the woman not to go to the police.

The brave woman ignored his pleas and notified cops of the sick attack as they identified the vehicle used to make the initial delivery.



Prajapati was taken into custody the same day as the accusations were first made.

He was arrested on suspicion of rape and non-fatal strangulation – a charge which was later dropped at court.

Prajapati of Castle Square, Wyberton West Road, Boston, appeared before Lincoln Crown Court on March 27.

He was sentenced to a five-year custodial sentence, reduced to three years and eight months after pleading guilty to rape.

He was also sentenced concurrently for 18 months for sexual assault and served with a deportation order.



Investigating the case, Detective Constable Jessica McKiernan, said: “Bringing this offender to justice was made possible by the extraordinary courage shown by the victim in coming forward at the earliest opportunity.

“Her trust in us allowed our officers to begin swift and focused inquiries, which led to the suspect being located within hours.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Her bravery has been vital in ensuring he is now held to account.

“We hope this outcome offers her some sense of reassurance as she moves forward on her own terms.”

News.title: Has this stripper revealed Trump’s Iran invasion plan? Exotic dancer says US troops are spilling secrets… & spending big

Charm Daze, a San Diego-based stripper with nearly a million followers on TikTok, told her army of followers that gloomy gunmen have been spending big ahead of their deployments to the Middle East.





San Diego is home to the largest US naval base on the West Coast – hosting Navy SEALs that could be used to seize key oil terminals on Kharg Island and free the Strait of Hormuz from Iran‘s iron grip.

But sombre soldiers have been putting Trump’s strategic mission in jeopardy by mistaking an exotic dancer for their therapist.

“Something I’ve noticed lately is all the military guys are coming in and they’re spending all of their money,” Daze says in the TikTok clip.

“It’s sad. They’re kind of depressed … They’re like, ‘Oh yeah, we’re gonna have fun, we’re getting deployed next week’.”

Daze goes on to describe the soldiers as kind and soft-spoken, making the experience all the more emotional for her.

“To see this young guys who look like my pinky toe, like fetuses, coming in and then dancing with them,” she says.

“It’s actually making me emotional. It’s f***ed up.”



The video quickly went viral, with viewers getting an inside look at the toll of bracing for a deployment to the Middle East.

But others pointed out that these troops were blowing operational security (OPSEC) and putting Trump’s bold invasion plan at risk.

“PSA: Don’t tell your adult entertainer you’re deploying,” Marine officer and influencer Kagan Dunlap posted on X.

“You gotta remind your folks: Don’t talk to your barber about when you’re deploying. Don’t talk to your adult entertainer about deploying or when you’re leaving, or what you’re doing or dates and times and locations.

“Because they don’t know any better, they’re gonna post a TikTok video about it.”

And 3,500 sailors and Marines aboard the USS Tripoli arrived over the weekend

In a fiery post on Truth Social, Trump said America is now in “serious discussions” with what he called a “new and more reasonable” regime in Tehran.



He hailed “great progress” and said a deal will “probably” be reached soon.

But he made it crystal clear the stakes couldn’t be higher.

Don warned that if Iran fails to agree – and if the Strait of Hormuz is not “immediately ‘Open for Business’”– the US will respond with overwhelming force.

He said America will conclude its “lovely ‘stay’ in Iran by blowing up and completely obliterating all of their Electric Generating Plants, Oil Wells and Kharg Island (and possibly all desalinization plants!), which we have purposefully not yet ‘touched’.”

News.title: Families to save £50 on holidays under Reform plan to scrap flying taxes, Nigel Farage pledges
News.content:
TURNING RIGHT Families to save £50 on holidays under Reform plan to scrap flying taxes, Nigel Farage pledges

FLYING taxes would be scrapped under a Reform government to make family holidays cheaper, Nigel Farage has pledged.

The party today promised to waive Air Passenger Duty for short-haul journeys as one of the first acts if elected.





Mr Farage said: “We believe that if you set your alarm, get up early and work hard then the government should give you a break.

“This Brexit benefit demonstrates the real difference a Reform government will make by putting money back in your pocket.”

Aspiring Chancellor Robert Jenrick said this would save the average family £45 for a flight to Europe.

Unveiling the announcement at Heathrow Airport, he said: “In our first budget we will get rid of the Family Holiday Tax.



“Air Passenger Duty will be gone for short-haul trips. If you were catching a plane to Malaga, you would save 23 per cent on the cost of your flights.

“Now we appreciate that’s not a huge amount of money, but it’s an important saving that will make it that bit easier to have that family trip, to have a bit of fun, to get away with your loved ones.”

Reform’s Treasury spokesman Mr Jenrick said APD would be scrapped for adults travelling with children under-18.

He blasted Chancellor Rachel Reeves for hiking the flying tax during the cost of living crisis.



From tomorrow APD will increase from £13 to £15 for an economy short-haul flight abroad.

Reform said the cost of scrapping the tax would be £120million and be funded out of £40billion of savings to the migrant and welfare bill.

A Heathrow spokesperson said: “Aviation is crucial to the UK’s economy and high levels of air passenger duty are a barrier to connectivity and our ability to compete internationally.

“We welcome any proposals that would reduce air passenger duty.”

A Labour spokesman said: “Nigel Farage has constantly jetted off around the world since becoming an MP, bagging hundreds of thousands of pounds for himself in the process. Reform are not on your side.



“Labour took the fair choice to hike tax on big private jets, which Farage opposed.

“Only this Labour is delivering a serious plan to ease the cost of living for families. From this week, the lowest earners will get a pay rise, pensions are going up, and energy bills being cut.“

News.title: Brit broadcast engineer, 74, found dead in hotel in India where he was working on IPL cricket coverage
News.content:
HOTEL TRAGEDY Brit broadcast engineer, 74, found dead in hotel in India where he was working on IPL cricket coverage

A BRITISH broadcast engineer working on Indian Premier League coverage has been found dead in a luxury Mumbai hotel.

The 74-year-old, who had been working with the Board of Control for Cricket in India, was discovered unresponsive in his room at the Trident Hotel.





He had checked in on March 24 while in the country for IPL 2026 coverage.

The engineer reportedly returned to his room after the Mumbai Indians vs Kolkata Knight Riders clash at Wankhede Stadium on March 29.

But when repeated calls to his room went unanswered the following day, alarmed hotel staff went to check on him.

After getting no response, staff allegedly used a master key to enter, where they found him lying on the floor.

The hotel’s in-house doctor was called and declared him dead at the scene.

Police have registered an accidental death report at Marine Drive Police Station, with investigations now underway.

Officials have not yet confirmed the cause of death.



The Sun has contacted the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office for more information.

The shock discovery has rocked those involved in the glitzy T20 tournament, coming just days into the new IPL season.

The tragedy also revives memories of former Australia cricketer Dean Jones, who died suddenly while working on IPL coverage in 2020.

It comes as other Brits have been found dead in hotel rooms abroad in recent months.

In Vietnam, a 25-year-old Brit was tragically found dead in a hotel room in Ho Chi Minh City.



Harleigh Jones, from Pontypridd, Wales, was sadly pronounced dead at the scene, on June 12 last year.

His death was later ruled “unnatural” at an inquest at Pontypridd Coroners Court.

A port-mortem reportedly found a mix of prescription drugs in his system, with a provisional cause of death linked to the combination of substances.

Funds have been raised in Mr Jones’ memory and donated to the Welsh charity 2Wish, which supports families who have lost a child.

Meanwhile in Thailand, a 21-year-old tourist was found dead in a Bangkok hotel just hours after being seen on a night out.



CCTV footage captured Joshua Kershaw in his final hours, where he was seen on a night out in the Thai capital.

He had earlier reportedly collapsed in a bar before returning to his room.

Bar staff suspected he had been eating too quickly and choked on his food.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Maids later discovered his body in the hotel room, with officers attempting to resuscitate Joshua before taking him away.

His cause of death is still unclear.

News.title: Teens accused of murdering Chloe Watson Dransfield appear in court as family weep
News.content:
Three teenagers charged with murdering a 16-year-old girl who was found with stab wounds to the back in a city street, have appeared in court where their family and friends were heard crying.

Chloe Watson Dransfield, from Gomersal, died in hospital following an incident in Kennerleigh Avenue, in the Austhorpe area of Leeds, at around 6am on Saturday.

Kayla Smith, 18, and Archie Rycroft, 19, both from Leeds, were charged with murder by West Yorkshire Police. A 17-year-old boy who cannot be named has also been charged with the same offence. All three were remanded in custody ahead of the appearance at Leeds Magistrates’ Court. The parents of all three accused were seen in court.

A force spokesman said another 18-year-old man, from Leeds, who was arrested on suspicion of murder remains in custody. An 18-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl, who were also arrested on suspicion of murder, have been released on bail pending further inquiries.

Image: ENTERPRISE NEWS AND PICTURES) ENTERPRISE NEWS AND PICTURES)

On Monday evening, Chloe’s father and other family members issued a tribute, saying they were “utterly devastated” and she would “never be forgotten”.

“We miss every single thing about her. She was beautiful, full of joy, and had a wonderfully cheeky personality,” they said.

“She embraced life with such happiness, and she had her whole future ahead of her. Chloe was loved by everyone who knew her, and the absence she leaves behind is immeasurable.

“We will miss her forever, she will never be forgotten. Love you always and forever, Dad, Sacha, Reuben, Mia, Amelia, Grandma, Grandad and Uncle Jordan.”

In a separate tribute, Chloe’s mother said she “cannot put into words” the loss of her “beautiful princess”.

"You are my life, my world, my best friend and I know that I am yours. I cannot live without you – I need you. You are stunning, confident, loyal, honest and my family-oriented princess.

"When you walk into any room it lights up with your bubbly personality. There is so much I could say. There’s a big hole in my heart that can never be filled.

"Your two sisters and big brother will always love and miss you to infinity. You will always and forever be in our hearts. Love Mum, Connor, Courtney and Cienna.”

Flowers were laid in the quiet street of bungalows and scenes-of-crime officers in white protective clothing were seen going into one of the homes on Monday. One of Chloe’s relatives has set up an online fundraising page which had raised nearly £15,000 by Tuesday morning.

News.title: Spain 13 airport strikes Tuesday update as aircraft take off 'without luggage'
News.content:
Spain 13 airport strikes Tuesday update as aircraft take off 'without luggage'

Passengers arrive to discover their posessions have been left behind as days of walkouts start at sites - full list

View Image Trolleys to transport suitcases in Terminal T4 of Adolfo Suarez Madrid-Barajas Airport, this Easter, as two ground handling strikes at Groundforce and Menzies airlines hit (Image: Getty Images)

Passengers flying from 13 Spanish airports hit by strike action have landed to discover all their luggage has been left behind, local media has reported. Canarias said the first day of the strike by Groundforce workers, the ground handling operator that services Air Europa flights, resulted in continuous delays across all the airline’s flights and passengers arriving at Canary Island airports without their luggage, having had to leave it behind at their point of origin.

‌



Alternating work stoppages are taking place between 5 and 7 am, 11 am and 5pm, and 10 pm and midnight, the first day of the strike affected 13 Spanish airports, three of them on the islands of Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, and Fuerteventura, where delays occurred throughout the day. These delays did not originate at the island airports but rather on flights arriving primarily from Madrid, Barcelona, and Bilbao, with delays approaching an hour.

‌



Airports impacted are Barcelona-El Prat, Madrid-Barajas, Ibiza, Palma de Mallorca, Gran Canaria, Tenerife, Fuerteventura, Bilbao, Lanzarote, Alicante, Valencia and Malaga. The Groundforce strike is scheduled for this Wednesday (April 1) and Good Friday (April 3), with the possibility of becoming indefinite.

‌



Because the aircraft operate on a network, delays accumulated throughout the day, causing significant disruptions to flights departing from the three affected airports in the archipelago. At major airports on the Iberian Peninsula, such as Madrid, Barcelona, and Bilbao, planes departed without luggage in their holds throughout Monday, leaving many passengers arriving at their destinations without their belongings.

Spain airport strikes warning as Easter travellers face severe delays READ MORE :

It’s worth remembering that the most affected route is Madrid-Gran Canaria, on which Air Europa operates seven flights daily. According to Orlando Robledano, secretary of the aviation sector at the UGT union, the strike’s impact on Canary Island airports has been reduced due to the minimum services imposed by Groundforce on all Lanzarote Airport employees. Even members of the works council received this notification requiring them to comply with these minimum services, making it impossible to achieve the level of participation required for a strike of this nature.

This, coupled with the fact that domestic flights at Canary Island airports are protected and must be serviced regardless of delays, meant that the problems were less severe at the islands’ airports than at those on the mainland. Other affected airports include Alicante, Valencia, Palma de Mallorca, Ibiza, and Málaga.

‌



Hosteltur reported that strikes at Canary Island airports during the peak days of Holy Week, between Maundy Thursday (April 2) and Easter Monday (April 6) may be called off as workers at Menzies—who provide check-in, boarding, and baggage services to airlines such as Norwegian, EasyJet, and British Airways—along with the works council and their union representatives from UGT, are close to reaching an agreement to call off the strike that was set to affect nearly 3,000 of the group’s employees in Spain, 600 of them in the Canary Islands.

At least six planes took off from Madrid-Barajas Airport on Monday without their passengers’ luggage due to an indefinite strike by the ground handling company Groundforce. On this first day of the strike, disruptions are being reported at all airports, although the most significant impacts are felt in Madrid and Barcelona, according to union sources, Telecinco reported.

Passengers report long queues and checked baggage left on the tarmac during the first day of the strike The indefinite strike by Groundforce ground staff began this Monday at Barcelona Airport, with protests taking place at three different times. The affected services are all those related to ground handling.

‌



Long queues were reported at Barcelona’s El Prat Airport, where Alberto García said: “There have been some delays, and some planes have even departed with very little luggage. It was the protesters themselves who informed passengers that their bags would not arrive on time.

“The unions continue fighting for their objective and are demanding that the company comply with the wage agreements stipulated in the collective bargaining agreement.” At this time, many people have seen their flights significantly delayed or have had their luggage left behind.

In Madrid, people have had to wait for extended periods to check their luggage. Some report waiting for “four or five hours.”

Article continues below

Many planes, especially those arriving from Madrid, “are arriving without luggage, and the problems are spreading,” a UGT spokesperson told Europa Press, adding that “there is no guarantee that luggage will arrive.” The delays “affect not only direct flights but also many connecting flights, since passengers arrive without their luggage and therefore miss their next flight.”

News.title: UK drivers getting up to £2,500 in compensation after going over potholes
News.content:
UK drivers getting up to £2,500 in compensation after going over potholes

Motorists could get £1,000s if they make a claim

View 2 Images MSE says whoever controls the road has a legal duty to do so correctly (stock image) (Image: Getty )

Some UK drivers who have put in a claim after a pothole caused damage to their car have been paid up to £2,500 in compensation, according to Money Saving Expert (MSE). Martin Lewis and his team of finance specialists at MSE say they've heard success stories from motorists who have received compensation payouts.

‌



One MSE reader, called Colin, said: "After looking at the guide on MSE... the result is that my car is now repaired and the council fully reimbursed me for my repair costs (over £2,500). This would have been so much harder if it hadn't been for your website, so thank you."

‌



Another said: "Two mangled alloys and one tyre, £735 worth of damage. Claim now settled for the full amount after initially being thrown out. Thank you MSE for the pothole claim guidelines."

‌



It comes as MSE put out a new post today (March 31), urging drivers to consider making a claim if their car is damaged after hitting a pothole. Taking to X, MSE said: "Don't let a hole in the road put a hole in your wallet."

It added: "The latest figures show there's a record £18 billion pothole repair backlog! But whoever controls the road has a legal duty to do so correctly – if they don't, they should pay for repairs."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Under the Highways Act 1980, the responsibility to maintain roads and the liability to pay for damages if they fail to do so generally rest with whoever controls the road, whether a public authority or a private landowner. Under Section 41 of the Act, the local Highway Authority has a duty to maintain highways maintainable at public expense.

If an accident occurs due to a failure to maintain these roads, for example, potholes, the authority is generally liable to pay compensation. However, authorities can escape liability under Section 58 of the Act if they can prove they took "reasonable" care to ensure the highway was safe, such as by having a proper inspection and repair system in place

Martin Lewis said: "Our usual campaigns are about reclaiming money you've wrongly paid – not damages, which this guide is about. A compensation culture is dangerous and we need be wary of this, especially when taxpayers are footing the bill. Yet the authorities have a legal duty to maintain roads so they're safe for everyone to use. If they don't and your car's damaged, they should help pay the costs to repair it.

‌



View 2 Images There's a record £18 billion backlog of damage to local roads in England and Wales

"It's important to understand you can only claim anyway if the authority responsible for the road has been negligent. So if a cannon ball drops off a truck, causing a pothole which two minutes later damages your car, you've no right to claim – there's nothing the authorities could've done to prevent that.

"Even if you are eligible to claim, you have a decision to make. Some argue that compensation deprives authorities of much-needed cash to fix roads – others that the more people pursue their rights, the more incentive there is for authorities to improve the roads to avoid dealing with claims.

‌



"After huge user demand to know pothole rights, we've delivered this guide for our users, we hope, in a responsible, non-militant, easy-to-use way. You must decide whether to use them."

What you need to make a claim

Before you can make a claim, MSE says there is criteria to check. It explains: "To be a pothole, it usually needs to be at least 4cm deep. You need to prove it was the pothole. Check who's responsible – then report it. You can claim if your vehicle's damaged and the authority responsible for the road failed to properly maintain it. If you've hit a pothole, consider telling your insurer."

‌



Drivers should gather evidence as soon as possible, as MSE says: " The first thing to do is start collecting proof, pronto. No matter which authority you're claiming from, the overall goal's the same – to gather enough evidence to prove its negligence."

This includes taking pictures of the pothole and measuring its depth, only if it is safe to do so. Also, MSE recommends taking pictures of your car and the damage, the pothole's position in the road, and any nearby road signs.

MSE says a 'fast claim' is the quickest way to claim. For this, you need to know which authority is responsible for the pothole you hit and have already reported it.

Article continues below

A statement on Gov.uk reads: "You may be able to claim compensation if your vehicle has been damaged by a road. The organisation you contact depends on where the road is and the type of road. You cannot claim compensation if debris from another vehicle caused the damage. Contact your insurer instead." Contact the organisation responsible to tell them:

News.title: 'Sea surrounded us in seconds - suddenly my daughter was swept away'
News.content:
'Sea surrounded us in seconds - suddenly my daughter was swept away'

Inaayah Makda, seven, from Blackburn, Lancs, was standing with her parents on rocks at a Casablanca beach when they were hit by a large wave - her body has yet to be found

View 2 Images Inaayah Makda (Image: MastersofMartialArtsB'burn/ SWNS)

A heartbroken dad has told how the ocean surrounded his family “within seconds” before his daughter was swept out to sea while on holiday in Morocco.

‌



Inaayah Makda, seven, from Blackburn, Lancs, was standing with her parents on rocks at a Casablanca beach when they were hit by a large wave on January 28. In an emotional video posted on social media, her father Zubair Makda told how the “water came gushing really fast” and “surrounded us as it came behind us”.

‌



He said the only “safe place” for them was to stand on the rocks. He said he glanced at Inaayah “and that was my last sight of her”, adding: “Within seconds the water came and took us out.”

‌



View 2 Images Inaayah's dad has told how the family were engulfed in second by the waves (Image: Handout)

Costa hotel explosion horror as dozens evacuated and smoke visible for miles READ MORE :

In the post, Zubair said Inaayah went missing on the first day of a five-day holiday. The family had landed in Rabat before travelling to Casablanca for two days to visit a mosque. Moments before the tragedy he was praying at a nearby cafe before he went to look for his wife and daughter.

‌



A massive search operation, which was hampered by bad weather, was called off by Moroccan authorities with no sign of Inaayah found. In the video Zubair told how he found his family at least 50 to 60 metres to the shoreline, saying “They were standing in the safe zone.”

As he reached the rocks, he said “suddenly within seconds water came gushing, extremely fast and it surrounded us and it came behind us. We had nowhere to go. Our only safe place was the rocks. So we stood on the rocks. Half a metre to a metre high.

“I looked at Inaayah and I glanced at her and that was my last sight of her. Within seconds the water came and took us out.” He said in total eight people were dragged into the sea. Zubair said he was in the water for “over a minute”, adding: “I felt like I was going to die that day. I must have crashed into another rock and that allowed me to get up.”

Article continues below

He said he then saw his wife, Tasneem, and pulled her from the sea: “As soon as I got her out we were looking for Inaayah straight away. And we couldn't find her. And at that point it was devastating." Zubair thanked everyone who had supported the family and helped in the search for the “bright, loving and gentle little girl”.

News.title: Michael Barrymore before TikTok - gruesome pool death, sedated wife and Diana
News.content:
Michael Barrymore before TikTok - gruesome pool death, sedated wife and Diana

Michael Barrymore is the Gen Z TikTok hit no-one saw coming, with 4.3million followers loving his taste tests and life in Devon. But before rebranding as a social media star, the former quiz show host hit rock bottom

View 8 Images Michael Barrymore has gained a whole new generation of fans on TikTok

Michael Barrymore is a Gen Z TikTok icon, but before social media, a tragedy imploded his life and left his TV career in tatters.

‌



The 73-year-old has amassed 4.3million followers on the platform, with videos documenting his new life in Devon, his love of Fortnite, shopping for snacks, and rating his KFC.

‌



Michael's followers love him, and are quick to comment on his videos - and he frequently replies. "I never skip a Barrymore vid!!" one recently wrote, while another said: "You really are living your best life right now and clearly loving it." Tellingly, the bio on Michael's page reads: "This is a very happy place to be…"

‌



It's something of a quiet resurgence for the Bermondsey-born star. Many of his younger followers might be unaware of Michael's past fame, and his public fall from grace in 2001.

Michael Barrymore provides health update to fans as he recovers from operation READ MORE :

View 8 Images Michael has 4.3million followers on TikTok and frequently posts videos on the platform

In the 1980s and 1990s, Michael – real name Michael Parker – was the king of British television, fronting popular shows such as Strike It Lucky, My Kind Of People, and a variety show. After a dip in viewing figures, he went on to present other programmes, including My Kind of Music and Kids Do the Funniest Things.

‌



But behind the scenes, Michael was battling alcohol and drug addictions, and received treatment in rehab. He wrote a 2006 book about his experiences, Awight Now: Setting the Record Straight.

Then, in 2001, the body of Stuart Lubbock was found floating in the swimming pool at Michael's Roydon home.

View 8 Images Stuart Lubbock was found dead in the entertainer's swimming pool in March 2001 (Image: PA)

‌



Stuart had been part of a group of people who had gone back to the house following a night out in nearby Harlow on 31 March 2001. His dad Terry Lubbock previously told the Guardian his son would have jumped at the chance to party with the star. "Stuart was a show-off - that was his weakness. He'd have gone straight up there to the house just so he could tell everyone about it the next day," he said.

The group was seen on CCTV catching a taxi back to the sprawling property at 2.30am, and Michael told a 2002 Epping inquest that despite not knowing Stuart, he "seemed a nice guy." He continued: "He was wandering in and out of various rooms [at my house] taking the place in. He seemed really happy."

Meanwhile, Stuart's friend Justin Merritt said he relaxed in the hot tub with Michael's former boyfriend, Jonathan Kenney, and watched Stuart splashing around, having fun in the pool. "He was the happiest person there, playing around, dancing and just mucking about," he told the inquest, which recorded an open verdict.

‌



View 8 Images The tragedy took place at Michael's £2million mansion in Roydon, Essex (Image: Channel 4)

But soon after at 5:46am the alarm was raised when Stuart's lifeless body was spotted in the pool. A postmortem later discovered he had sustained severe internal injuries. Police did not treat the house as a crime scene, at first believing that Stuart had drowned after drinking heavily and taking cocaine and ecstasy. But a murder probe was launched after an examination found he had suffered major internal injuries and cardiac arrest.

Rumours of group sex flew, but Stuart's father Terry Lubbock said his son identified as heterosexual and would not have entered into a same-sex experience. Mr Merritt also insisted he was with Stuart for all but a tiny fraction of the night. "When I look back now, he was really happy... He wasn't in any discomfort like anyone had messed with him or touched him," he continued.

‌



"There was no time (it could have happened). He was with us (in the hot tub), then in the pool. Then he went away. That was the only time he wasn't around. That was the only time we never really saw him or knew what he was doing. There wasn't a time when it could have happened."

View 8 Images No-one has been charged in relation to Stuart's death (Image: PA)

By the time police arrived, TV star Michael had left the property - a move he later admitted was the "worst thing I could have done." He told Radio 5 Live's Stephen Nolan Show he "freaked out" after seeing Stuart "floating in the pool" and ran back into the house to find a guest with life saving experience.

‌



"I didn't run away - first thing I did was go and get help. I was standing there and instead of going, 'I should stay here,' I went with the lads down the bottom of their drive to their flat. As I went out I rang my PA - I've never had a PR agent - and said a guy's by the side of the pool - the ambulance has been called if the police need me I'm in James' place at the bottom of the drive."

Admitting his actions "absolutely" didn't look good, he maintained his innocence and insisted the injuries did not happen at the party.

"No way did I do it. And if I did then I'd have put my hands up 10 years ago. I haven't spoken about this like this probably really at all to be honest," he said. "I do find it difficult to talk about. Not because I'm guilty of anything but because I didn't do anything I did a stupid thing - I walked away from the scene but I'd already gone and got help to bring him out. Nothing happened to the guy there."

‌



View 8 Images The late Princess Diana was good friends with Michael Barrymore (Image: UK Press via Getty Images)

The entertainer and two other men were arrested in 2007 on suspicion of sexual assault and murder but were later released without charge. Michael has always denied involvement in Stuart's death.

"I could not be more sorry that this event took place," he told Piers Morgan. "I gave Stuart nothing. There were no E's at my house. I had a joint. If there was cocaine he didn't get it from me. Stuart's family deserve proper answers and the police have not completed their inquiries properly."

‌



View 8 Images Michael has always maintained his innocence (Image: PA)

The High Court ruled years later that Michael's arrest was unlawful because the arresting officer did not have reasonable grounds to suspect him. And in 2009, the police watchdog published the findings of a review of the investigation into Stuart's death, concluding that officers missed crucial evidence and did not ensure vital forensic tests were completed until six years later.

Police have re-investigated the case multiple times, including arrests in 2021 based on "significant new information," but no charges have been brought.

‌



Essex Police said they have never - and would never - stop searching for answers. In 2023, a spokesman said "Essex Police has never shied away from the fact that, at the time of the original incident, the scene was not preserved or secured as quickly as it could have been to ensure the best forensic evidence was obtained.

"However, what remains certain is that Essex Police has never given up on finding out exactly what happened to Stuart, and we will continue to act on any new information to assist us in our pursuit of justice for him and for his family and friends.

"As we have said repeatedly over the last 20 years, nine people were at that party. We know that not everyone was responsible for what happened, but someone was. Now is the time to come forward, if you haven't done so already, to set this matter to rest by providing us with any information you have."

‌



View 8 Images The TV star married Cheryl Cocklin in 1976 (Image: Kevin Holt/Daily Mail/REX/Shutterstock)

Michael came out as gay in 1995, and left the home he shared with his wife. He had met Cheryl Cocklin in 1974 while she was a dancer in a West End theatre show, and they married in 1976.

In August 1995, at the height of his fame, Barrymore went to The White Swan gay pub in London's East End, where he gave an impromptu stage performance, singing the words: "Start spreading the news, I'm gay today", in the style of the "Theme from New York, New York". Two days later, it was on the cover of every tabloid newspaper.

‌



Cheryl had to be sedated, such was her devastation, and the shock plunged her into menopause. "I became very ill," she once told The Standard. "My weight dropped to five stone and I couldn't keep any food down. I was not very big to start with, so I must have looked terrible. I was heavily sedated and had no will to live. I didn't have the energy to do anything. I didn't know where I was. I'd lost my husband, my career, everything, all in one go."

In the years following the breakup there have been suggestions that Cheryl must have known her husband was gay. It is a suggestion she fiercely rejects. "I've always resented being lumped in with those women who knew really, but turned a blind eye. I'm not one of them, I didn't know."

The Strike It Lucky star later claimed his rebellion was sparked by a need to break free of being a "clothes horse" - and revealed that his number one backer was Princess Diana.

‌



"Her original comment was that she was glad when I was in the papers because it kept her off the front page," he previously told the Guardian of their unlikely bonding. He continued: "She was one who said you've got to stop being controlled. By that stage, I was just a clothes-horse. It got to the point where I would never look in the mirror even before I went out on stage - I just accepted what they had put on me."

The rebellion began with the once squeaky-clean star falling out of nightclubs and award ceremonies drunk. He explained: "I had to be Mr Clean, right down to not a hair on my head being out of place, what jumper I wore, the way I walked. And eventually I just thought: I want to be naughty."

Diana is said to have been one of the first to know of Michael's true sexuality and encouraged him to embrace it. When he was admitted to rehab in 1996, Diana apparently left a holiday early to return to London to comfort him. But for Cheryl - who died from cancer in 2005 - their closeness was unnerving.

‌



In her autobiography Catch a Falling Star she wrote: "[Diana] seemed to believe they could achieve something truly great and immortal together because they had the key to weeping massive public affection."

And when Diana was killed in a car accident in Paris in 1997, distraught Michael called his wife from a Brixton gay club begging her to tell him it wasn't true. "I went round there in the afternoon and she was seeing Dodi [Fayed] at the time and she said, 'I'm going to Paris tonight. I'll see you and the boys on Wednesday,'" he told Piers Morgan's Life Stories of their last ever meeting. "And that never happened. She died."

The entertainer also believes Diana could have saved him from his drink and drug demons. He explained: "I have a feeling that if she was around it wouldn't have been so bad... she would have helped me through it."

News.title: Couple 'kept woman as slave' and 'fed her only Weetabix' before she died
News.content:
Couple 'kept woman as slave' and 'fed her only Weetabix' before she died

Chee Kit Chong and Angie Yeh Liaw are accused of forcing a woman to be their domestic 'slave' - with the husband alleged to have beaten her when she failed to carry out household chores

View 2 Images Chee Kit Chong and wife Angie Yeh Ling Liaw are accused of keeping a woman as a house 'slave' (Image: Facebook)

A married couple has been accused of keeping a woman as a live-in 'slave' and feeding her a diet of only Weetabix before she died.

‌



Chee Kit Chong and Angie Yeh Liaw have pleaded not guilty to slavery charges after an Indonesian woman was allegedly beaten, deprived of food, and forced to sleep on the stairs during her 10-month ordeal. The woman, who was in Australia illegally, was supposed to stay for only a month in early 2022, Victorian County Court heard.

‌



But she was allegedly blamed by Mr Chong for losing a company credit card and told she must work off the debt.

‌



View 2 Images Police were called by a nurse after she noticed injuries on the woman's body, a court heard (file photo) (Image: Getty Images)

British mum's heartbreaking note before falling to death from Thailand balcony READ MORE :

Chong and Liaw, who are originally from Malaysia, then "heavily controlled" the alleged victim's life, prosecutors said, forcing her to provide "domestic services" and keeping her in squalid conditions. The alleged victim (who has not been named) died in 2024, though this is not related to the case.

Today, a jury was told that the alleged victim was told she could "only eat Weet-Bix" - an Australian breakfast cereal similar to Weetabix - as she cleaned the family's home and looked after their children without pay. Prosecutor Shaun Ginsbourg SC said: "Mr Chong threatened and coerced (the victim) to provide domestic services, repeatedly told her she had to work to repay supposed debts.

‌



"When (the victim) failed at her duties, or failed to complete them to Chong's satisfaction, he would often hit or kick her, or punish her by telling her she could not sleep or eat that day."

In one incident described to the court, Chong allegedly hit the woman with a vacuum cleaner after she fell asleep while giving him a leg massage. P rosecutors also claim he made her stand up all night without sleep as punishment for failing to do tasks, and on another occasion locked her in the garage.

The court heard that Chong explained away her injuries to doctors by claiming she had been attacked by a homeless man, and that she had diabetes. An investigation was launched after a nurse went to the police.

Article continues below

Chong is accused of using the woman as a slave, while his wife is charged with assisting or encouraging the offence, reported the Newcastle Herald. The husbands's defence lawyers have disputed many details surrounding the case, including claims of abuse, sleep, and food deprivation, as well as the allegations about the forced 'repayment' of the credit card.

He also denied ordering her to do tasks, saying it was the woman's own idea. "There may be reasons [the woman] may exaggerate or embellish or say things that are untruthful," Chong's defence lawyer Diana Price said.

The trial continues.

News.title: Woman gets big surprise after turning up for 'scenic boat ride' husband booked
News.content:
Woman gets big surprise after turning up for 'scenic boat ride' husband booked

Couple George & Crissa Prieto regularly share videos from their travel escapades on Instagram, In one of their latest reels, Crissa revealed how her idea of a nice boat ride was a bit different to what she got on her New Zealand break

View 2 Images She thought she was getting a 'scenic' boat ride (stock image) (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Most of us love going on a little boat ride when on an overseas break. Getting out on the ocean can be a great way to relax and top up your tan usually. However, one woman got a big surprise when she turned up for the 'scenic boat ride' her husband booked while on a trip to New Zealand.

‌



George & Crissa Prieto, who brand themselves an 'adventure travel couple', regularly share videos from their travel escapades on Instagram with their 642,000 followers. In one of their latest reels, Crissa revealed how her idea of a nice boat ride was a bit different to what she got on her New Zealand break.

‌



The clip saw Crissa get into a shark-shaped jet boat as overlay text read, 'POV: Your husband books you a "scenic boat ride" then realises that means something very different in New Zealand...'

‌



She was seen waving before she got into the boat, however her expression soon turned tense as she whizzed along the water and the jet jumped into the air.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

However, after the initial shock, Crissa seems to settle in and thoroughly enjoy her wild ride as she smiled into the camera.

‌



Following up in the caption, Crissa wrote: "Did you know you can race across Lake Wakatipu in Queenstown, New Zealand in a shark-shaped jet boat that dives, spins, and launches through the water?!

"Strapping yourself into this $100,000 (£76,000) semi-submersible shark is hands-down one of the most adrenaline-filled experiences in New Zealand!"

She added: "This experience was unreal! Rocketing across the lake at high speed, plunging underwater, breaching up to 15ft in the air, and taking in the dramatic mountain scenery… this is truly one of the most unique bucket list experiences in the world.

‌



"Who would you ride the HydroAttack with?!"

View 2 Images It was a different boat to what she expected (Image: BOOKME)

Crissa revealed that they paid $125 NZD (£54) per person for the experience, but said prices may vary by the season.

‌



Trips last 15 minutes total on the water and there is no experience needed to ride. "Just be ready for speed, splashes, and serious adrenaline," she wrote. "You’ll be riding with a trained pilot the whole time."

People were loving the post, with it racking up more than 115,000 likes.

One person exclaimed: "This is awesome," while another added: "So cool!"

Article continues below

A third quipped: "Best scenic ride ever."

News.title: Inside terrifying craze that sees boys smash their faces with hammers for 'perfect look'
News.content:
Inside terrifying craze that sees boys smash their faces with hammers for 'perfect look'

In recent years, a dangerous trend known as 'looksmaxxing' has taken social media by storm, and young boys as young as 10 are reportedly using hammers to chisel the 'perfect jawline'

View 6 Images Braden Eric Peters is known online as Clavicular (Image: clavicular0/Instagram )

Young men desperate to attract girlfriends are going to extreme measures to achieve the “perfect look” — by smashing their own faces with hammers.

‌



The internet streamer at the centre of the health craze is a man called Braden Eric Peters — known by fans as Clavicular — and earlier this week he was arrested on a battery charge.

‌



Controversial Clavicular, 20, was accused of instigating a fight between two women before posting what happened on social media. He has since been released from custody.

‌



And while the self-entitled “misogynist influencer”, who claims he is now infertile from injecting himself with steroids, may not be a name familiar to many, it certainly is with a lot of young people. He built his following based on a movement known as looksmaxxing.

If you are unsure of what this means, it is essentially about maximising physical attractiveness, and sometimes drastically altering your appearance by any means necessary.

View 6 Images Braden Eric Peters with a hammer (Image: X/@wyabalenci)

‌



Young lads are going to bizarre lengths to achieve this, including using hammers to chisel more aesthetically pleasing jawlines.

And when Clavicular, who now has more than one million followers across his social media accounts, was a teenage boy, his own mum had to get rid of the hammer from their home, just so her son would stop smashing his own face up.

However, despite ordering testosterone and fat dissolvers online aged just 14, his parents eventually realised “there was nothing that they could do to stop my ascension”, as reported in The New York Times.

‌



According to reports, little boys as young as 10 years old are now getting their hands on hammers in the hopes of a chiseled jawline.

But Clavicular, who was expelled from school for testosterone possession and has since partied with Andrew Tate, didn’t just stop at “bone-smashing”. He has also been on record telling his impressionable young followers that he lost weight after his appetite was suppressed thanks to smoking crystal meth — something known as leanmaxxing.

View 6 Images It is beauty at all costs for Clavicular (Image: Instagram/ @clavicular0)

‌



Looksmaxxing meanwhile is said to help young men achieve ultimate beauty — and less extreme techniques include working out and having skincare and grooming routines.

Insecure boys and young men are finding harmful looksmaxxing content on online forums where they can be advised to seek leg extension surgery if they are not deemed tall enough.

The looksmaxxing forums took off in the 2010s but rather than being on the fringe of the internet, it is now discussed by influencers on platforms like TikTok and Instagram.

‌



Influencers share before and after pictures and this is said to encourage others to take similar risks to improve their looks.

View 6 Images He has gone to extreme measures to look how he looks (Image: Instagram/ @clavicular0)

Another term that has come out is hardmaxxing — which is the more extreme measures to achieve beauty including Botox and steroids.

‌



One expert claimed such measures were making people feel resentful of themselves — and can even lead to suicides.

Michael Halpin, who is an Associate Professor of Sociology, told The Sun: “I observed a teenager stating that he was going to take his own life if he did not reach 6ft in height.

“While other users were told they were too ugly for ‘ooksmaxxing and they should consider suicide. They are told they need to looksmax if they want to look better or ‘normal.”

‌



However, it is not just men getting hooked on looksmaxxing, and the Mirror once spoke to a young woman who became brainwashed by the same trend.

View 6 Images Kseniya Didik (Image: Kseniya Didik)

Russian woman Kseniya Didik, who was 21 when she spoke exclusively with this publication, warned people about the “addictive” trend that she became obsessed with in her teenage years.

‌



Sharing her story, she said: “I’ve always been insecure about not fitting in, I guess. I was bigger than most girls at five, then I was the only one with acne, then I was the late bloomer-ugly duckling in a class full of beautiful girls in high school.

“I started taking part in beautifying rituals around 12... I also slipped into eating disorder territory around the same time, because I thought I was so big and ugly compared to other girls, when looking back, I wasn’t even big...

“But really looksmaxxing has always been present in my life, consciously and subconsciously – from the women in my family having rigorous skincare, makeup and dieting routines to magazine tips and permeating advertising. So, I’d probably engage in it regardless of circumstance.”

‌



View 6 Images Kseniya shared her thoughts on looksmaxxing (Image: Kseniya Didik)

Before she turned 18, Kseniya often had pore extractions and laser resurfacing to help with acne scars, and she was desperate to one day after lip filler, eye bag surgery and a nose job.

However, her dangerous dieting led to her menstrual cycle stopping at one point. Looksmaxxing is now widely linked to the ‘manosphere’ and the term has also been used during discussions about incels.

‌



But Kseniya said: “I really don’t like how looksmaxxing has essentially been co-opted and rebranded for men. It’s pretty much the same thing women have done for ages, now with a 'for men' sticker and a layer of self-deprecation and pseudo-science behind it.

“I sought out communities specifically for women, or centred around specific issues, and they're nothing like that. Just a group of like-minded people sharing their experiences and trying to help each other.”

Counsellor Georgina Sturmer meanwhile spoke about the perils of looksmaxxing and advised: “If we are drawn towards [this]... it’s likely that there are some strong underlying emotional motivations.

Article continues below

“We might be struggling with our self-esteem, feeling anxious, depressed or isolated. Or we might find ourselves trying to regain a sense of control when everything around us feels overwhelming... There are plenty of organisations out there who are ready and willing to help.”

Dr Lawrence Cunningham, a GP at the UK Care Guide, added: “Maintaining physical appearance through healthy lifestyle choices is normal and can be beneficial. However, the line should be drawn when such practices become extreme and harmful.

“Building a network of positive influences, whether through friends, family, or professional counsellors, can make a significant difference in one's mental and physical health.”
